item.title: Yari never called Nigerian youths lazy – Group insists
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Senator Yari National Unity Project for Tinubu 2027 has dismissed reports that Senator Abdul’aziz Abubakar Yari described Nigerian youths as lazy, accusing sections of the media of misrepresenting his remarks at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State. The group said Yari, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, was speaking about hunger, food availability and the dignity of hard work, rather than disparaging young Nigerians. In a statement issued by its National Coordinator, Dr Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi, the group challenged those circulating the allegation to watch the full footage of Yari’s address, insisting that the senator had acknowledged the economic hardship facing Nigerians before making his remarks on productivity. “He opened his remark by stating plainly: ‘We have hunger.’ At no point in that remark did the Senator mention, single out or describe Nigerian youths. To turn a statement on the dignity of work, made by a man who had just acknowledged that hunger exists, into the headline ‘Yari calls youths lazy’ is not reporting; it is spin,” the statement said. To support its position, the group cited Yari’s interventions in education, military recruitment, agriculture and public-sector employment, arguing that his record demonstrated his commitment to the welfare and empowerment of young Nigerians. It also claimed that Yari facilitated the enlistment of 158 young people from Zamfara West into two Nigerian Army recruitment intakes and supported farmers with agricultural inputs and equipment. “A leader who sends thousands of young people to university and into national service does not hold Nigerian youths in contempt; he invests in them,” the statement added. The group reaffirmed its confidence in Yari and directed its officers nationwide to intensify grassroots mobilisation for President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. It also urged media organisations that published the disputed report to review the full footage of the senator’s address and correct what it described as a misrepresentation. “Political disagreement is legitimate; misrepresentation is not,” the statement added. The post Yari never called Nigerian youths lazy – Group insists appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: Think of TK as Google Docs meets group chats, meets blogging. | Image: David Pierce / The Verge For the first time ever, Medium is becoming more than just a blogging platform. item.title: 2027: Any Igbo against Obi is enemy of Ndigbo – Victor Umeh
item.description: Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central Senatorial District, has declared that any Igbo person opposed to the presidential ambition of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Peter Obi, is an enemy of Ndigbo. Umeh, who described Obi as the conscience of the Igbo people, also cautioned political leaders in the South-East, particularly the Anambra State Government, against working against the former governor’s presidential ambition ahead of the 2027 general elections. The senator, popularly known as Ohamadike, made the remarks in a trending video, on Monday. He said Obi represented the collective aspirations of the Igbo people and urged the people of the South-East to rally behind him. “I’m an Igbo activist, you people know me and you hear my voice in the Senate on all issues of national importance. Peter is our conscience in this election. Any Igbo man who stands up to say we will not vote for Peter Obi, I’m telling you that he’s an enemy of Igbo people,” Umeh said. He specifically warned the Anambra State Government against allegedly opposing Obi’s ambition for political reasons, arguing that the state’s leadership should consider the broader interests of the Igbo people. Umeh claimed he played a significant role in the emergence of Governor Chukwuma Soludo, insisting that the office of governor was held in trust for the collective interest of the people. “This government in the state, I helped installing it. Nobody came here the governor of Anambra State since 2003 without my input. This one that is serving, I was a principal contributor to his ascending to that office. He’s holding that office on trust for all of us,” he said. The senator urged Soludo not to undermine Obi’s presidential ambition, describing any attempt to work against his kinsman as an abomination. “Let him not commit what is called abomination by wanting to destroy his brother in the name of politics,” he warned. Umeh further argued that if politicians from other geopolitical zones were free to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu, Igbo people should equally be allowed to rally behind Obi without intimidation or condemnation. Recalling Obi’s support for him, the senator called on Ndigbo to stand for what he described as truth and justice, adding that Obi’s success in the 2027 presidential election would be a collective achievement for the South-East. “He told me this is his time and if he makes it, the Igbos have made it. So let nobody come and insult us and our intelligence,” Umeh added. The post 2027: Any Igbo against Obi is enemy of Ndigbo – Victor Umeh appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: The moment Mercedes’ glorious F1 comeback started? How about their lowest-ever ebb
item.description: “One of my worst days in racing,” proclaimed an aghast Toto Wolff . The scene is the paddock at the Bahrain International Circuit, the date is March 2023 and the occasion is the aftermath of the season-opening Formula One race. Mercedes have just finished more than 50 seconds off the pace set by winner Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, with Lewis Hamilton in fifth and George Russell in seventh. Behind three other cars, the former untouchable giants of F1 are, clearly, the fourth-quickest car on the grid . And in that moment, Wolff realises that – once again – he and his team of engineers and car designers back at their Brackley base have got it badly wrong. It’s worth revisiting the Silver Arrows at their lowest ebb as we revert back to the present day. On Sunday, Mercedes claimed the F1 constructors’ crown for the first time in five years, a week on from their first drivers’ world championship in six years. It is a ninth teams’ title for Mercedes, putting them level with Williams and placing them one behind McLaren on the all-time list. For Wolff, too, it puts him level with Frank Williams for the most titles for a team boss in F1 history. Mercedes celebrate in Sao Paulo (PA) Not bad, then, given the desperate doldrums the Austrian executive found himself in nearly four years ago. That day in Bahrain marked the start of this new era. A year earlier, amid the new ground-effect rule change off the back of that 2021 decider in Abu Dhabi , Mercedes’ zero-sidepod design caught the attention of everyone up and down the pit lane. And yet, as action began on the track, not only were they short of top-table pace, but their car was violently oscillating in a phenomenon called “porpoising” that nobody at HQ had envisaged. So much so that, after one race in Baku, Hamilton struggled to disembark the cockpit, such was the pain in his back. But Russell’s inaugural victory in F1 at Interlagos – Mercedes’ first win of the 2022 season, on a weekend where they claimed a one-two finish – presented a lifeline. Or so they thought at the time. Wolff has since acknowledged that it was that win which pushed Mercedes to continue down the zero-sidepod path. In a holistic game of stick-and-twist – with a rule phase not ending until 2026 – the three-pronged star decided to stick. It would prove to be a foolhardy decision. Despite seven grands prix triumphs between 2023-2025, Mercedes were still some way short of their competitors: first Red Bull, then McLaren. The three years since were something of a purgatory for Wolff who, to his credit, has never been one for hiding his emotions or ducking out of camera range in the garage, often to the detriment of a nearby headset. "Looking back in retrospect, you're saying, 'we needed these tough moments in order to grow as people or to grow as an organisation’ – but when you're down, that is quite difficult to feel,” he said on Sunday night, another constructors’ title in his back pocket. item.title: Who’s the Detroit News Boys High School Team of the Week? Vote now!
item.description: Every week, Michigan high school teams across the state are winning championships, breaking records, reaching milestones and putting together seasons worth celebrating. The Detroit News is recognizing those standout squads as Team of the Week. From nominations submitted by coaches, parents and fans, we’ve selected five boys teams as this week’s finalists. Any boys team, in any sport and from any region of Michigan, is eligible. Now it’s your turn to decide who deserves the honor. Voting is open from 10 a.m. Monday through 5 p.m. Thursday. Readers can vote multiple times, so rally your school community and get everyone involved. More: Subscribe to “Michigan Sidelines,” our high school sports newsletter The winner will be announced Friday morning in a special Detroit News post celebrating its accomplishments. Who deserves to be named the Detroit News Boys Team of the Week? Cast your vote below. Birmingham Seaholm boys tennis Birmingham Seaholm didn't just repeat as Division 2 boys tennis state champion. It dominated the competition, winning 35 matches at the state finals, the most of any program. Seaholm claimed five flight championships, with all eight flights advancing to at least the semifinals. Senior Kalil Wahab and freshman Hunter Helfman went unbeaten in five matches, winning every one in straight sets. That included a 7-6 (1), 6-4 victory in the No. 1 doubles final. Sophomore Charlie Griffith also came through, winning his second consecutive individual title at No. 3 singles. He battled through a three-set final, 6-2, 5-7, 6-3, and finished the season with a 20-4 record. It was another dominant performance for a program that continues to set the standard in Division 2. Holland Calvary Christian boys cross country Holland Calvary Christian didn't leave much doubt about who belonged at the top of Division 4 boys cross country. The team put all five scorers in the top 15 Saturday at Michigan International Speedway, cruising to its second consecutive state championship with 35 points. No boys team in any division scored better at the state finals. Senior Noah Schipper led the way with a fifth-place finish in 16:03.7. Senior Christian Getz wasn't far behind, taking seventh in 16:06.1. Senior Brody Van Tuinen also delivered, finishing 12th to earn his first All-State honor. With all five scorers in the top 15, Holland Calvary Christian put together one of the day's most impressive performances and defended its state championship in convincing fashion. Troy boys soccer Troy put together a season nobody else in Michigan boys soccer could match. The team finished 19-0-2, becoming the state's only unbeaten boys soccer program. It capped its historic run with a 2-1 victory over Livonia Stevenson in the Division 1 state championship Saturday at Grand Ledge High School. It was Troy's second state championship and first since 2003. Senior defender Faris Ibrahim and sophomore midfielder Connor Hotts each scored on a set piece in the championship game. Hot

item.title: Who’s the Detroit News Girls High School Team of the Week? Vote now!
item.description: Every week, Michigan high school teams across the state are winning championships, breaking records, reaching milestones and putting together seasons worth celebrating. The Detroit News is recognizing those standout squads as Team of the Week. From nominations submitted by coaches, parents and fans, we’ve selected five girls teams as this week’s finalists. Any girls team, in any sport and from any region of Michigan, is eligible. Now it’s your turn to decide who deserves the honor. Voting is open from 10 a.m. Monday through 5 p.m. Thursday. More: Subscribe to “Michigan Sidelines,” our high school sports newsletter The winner will be announced Friday morning in a special Detroit News post celebrating its accomplishments. Who deserves to be named the Detroit News Girls Team of the Week? Cast your vote below. Ann Arbor Pioneer girls cross country Ann Arbor Pioneer didn't just win its second consecutive Division 1 girls cross country state championship Saturday at Michigan International Speedway. It swept the top three individual spots, too. Pioneer finished with 87 points, led by junior Natasza Dudek, who captured her second straight individual state title in 16:26.6. That's the second-fastest time in state finals history. Sophomore Keira Von Blon finished runner-up in 16:49.8, while junior Sienna Klemmer took third in 16:54.7. Their times rank fifth and seventh, respectively, on the all-time state finals list. It was a historic day for Pioneer, which continues to set the standard in Division 1. Otsego girls cross country Otsego finally got its championship moment. After finishing runner-up in 2023 and 2025, Otsego captured the Division 2 girls cross country state championship Saturday at Michigan International Speedway with 84 points. No girls team scored better at the state finals. Sophomore twin sisters Alayna and Adelyn Verhage led the way, finishing 13th and 26th, respectively. Both recorded personal-best times on the biggest stage of the season. Sophomore Addelyn Sabatke added another top-30 finish, placing 28th in 18:34.1. Otsego had three All-State runners finish in the top 30, securing the program's fourth state championship. Ann Arbor Pioneer field hockey Ann Arbor Pioneer has made winning state championships look routine. Pioneer finished 18-3 and captured its second consecutive Michigan High School Athletic Association field hockey state championship, continuing a remarkable run under coach Jane Nixon. The team didn't lose to a Michigan opponent all season. All three losses came against out-of-state competition. And when the postseason arrived, Pioneer was nearly untouchable, shutting out opponents in all five playoff games while outscoring them 20-0. That included a 1-0 victory over Saline in the state championship game Oct. 31 at Michigan State's Ralph Young Field. item.title: Jonathan Taylor trade rumors: Giants deal unlikely as Colts star says goodbye to fans
item.description: Jonathan Taylor’s time with the Colts is coming to an end, and everyone knows it. The team is entering a complete teardown and rebuild, meaning that after six-and-a-half seasons the running back effectively said goodbye to the fans on Sunday following the team’s loss to Dallas. "I appreciate them and it was a pleasure to put on display all of not only my hard work, but the team's hard work." @ADChernoff asked Jonathan Taylor what he hopes the fans will remember about him if this is Taylor's last game with the #Colts : pic.twitter.com/Z6bL4IMT0M — WISH-TV News (@WISHNews8) November 8, 2026 Taylor appeared destined to become the No. 1 rusher in franchise history, needing only a shade over 1,000 yards to pass Edgerrin James. Instead, he will be locked in second place, remembered fondly as a no-nonsense rusher who kept the Colts afloat during some of their most difficult times in the post-Andrew Luck era. A constant throughout the noise, the big question remaining is “where will he go?” and here’s the latest being reported on where Taylor could end up. New York Giants The Giants are reportedly out on the idea of making a deal for Taylor. They are turning their attention towards a need on the interior defensive line, and would rather make a move there — according to Jordan Raanan of ESPN . Taylor would have been a huge addition to a team in need of running help, but it seems the Giants are more convinced that Cam Skattebo can bounce back from injury, and with a bolstered interior DL presence they will be set for a playoff run. The Colts are poised to take whatever the best offer in on Tuesday Pro Football Talk has reported that Indianapolis are set on trading Taylor, which likely precipitated his comments on Sunday — knowing he would be going somewhere this week. Seemingly, the Colts have no preference on where he might end up, simply being willing to deal him to whoever gives them the best offer . It had previously been reported that Indianapolis was looking for a haul like Carolina received for Christian McCaffrey. That trade netted a 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th round pick — though it seems increasingly unlikely the Colts will get as much as that deal. A handful of teams could make a trade for Taylor The Vikings are garnering a lot of attention when it comes to Taylor as a means to mitigate their woeful passing game San Francisco is a dark horse candidate to shore-up their offense in case Christian McCaffrey can’t remain healthy Cleveland could be a team to watch considering they are within striking distance of the AFC North’s top, and Quinshon Judkins has been inconsistent The Patriots will be another team to watch. Their lack of a reliable run game has put too much pressure on Drake Maye to carry the offense. A legitimate three-down back could make a huge impact for them

item.title: U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too FinCEN and the Federal Reserve have formally withdrawn a 2020 proposal that would have cut the Bank Secrecy Act threshold for cross-border funds transfers from $3,000 to $250 and spelled out that the rules cover crypto, leaving the existing $3,000 line in place. The notice, published Monday in the Federal Register, says the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and the Fed’s Board of Governors “will not take further action” on a proposal they first issued on Oct. 27, 2020. That plan would have lowered the recordkeeping and Travel Rule thresholds to $250 for transfers that begin or end outside the United States. Those rules require banks and nonbank financial institutions to collect, retain and pass along customer information on transfers of $3,000 or more. It also would have clarified the meaning of “money” in both rules so they apply to transactions involving convertible virtual currency, along with digital assets that have legal tender status to a recipient. Why the agencies backed off Per the notcie, FinCEN and the Fed received nearly 3,000 comments on the proposal, most of them substantially similar form letters. Commenters generally opposed the lower threshold, arguing that it would burden smaller institutions and could push consumers sending remittances toward less regulated channels. Many also noted that potentially illicit transfers below $3,000 were already being flagged to FinCEN through suspicious activity reports. Several said the threshold should rise instead, citing inflation since 1995. Sentiment on the crypto language was mixed. Companies that provide crypto services and their trade groups opposed it, citing technical limits and the lack of an international messaging standard for crypto transfers, while some banks and money services businesses supported it. The agencies gave two reasons for pulling the proposal. More than five years have passed, and they said more public feedback would help before adopting anything similar. The withdrawal, they wrote, gives the public “certainty” that no final rule will be issued without another chance to comment. The second reason is the crypto industry itself. The notice says crypto markets “have continued to mature” and new legal frameworks are emerging, citing the GENIUS Act stablecoin law enacted on July 18, 2025. Any future change tied to crypto, the agencies said, should be considered in light of those developments so it is “fit for purpose.” What the withdrawal does and does not do The notice does not repeal or amend any rule. The $3,000 threshold that has applied for decades stays where it is, and so does the existing Travel Rule. What disappears is the specific path to $250 and the proposed wording that would have written crypto into the definition of money. The agencies did not say whether they plan a new proposal or offer a timeline. The withdrawal is the latest in a run of reversals from Treasury. On Oct.

item.title: How to shop like a pro during Black Friday and Cyber Monday
item.description: Despite Amazon and other retailers filling the summer and fall months with more sales than ever before, Black Friday and Cyber Monday remain the biggest shopping days of the year. And, in recent years, the sale periods have started earlier, giving you more time to take advantage of the deals. We’re already hard at work to find the best prices on phones, accessories, 4K TVs, noise-canceling headphones, gaming gear, and other tech throughout the deal-packed weeks culminating in the big events, whether you plan to shop in person or online. You can always count on us to publish only the best deals that you need to know about , no matter the season. However, if you want to be among the first people to spot price drops on the products you’re interested in, you’ll want to get a head start on your Black Friday and Cyber Monday game plan. Thankfully, we have a few suggestions for scouting early sales at your favorite retailers, finding the right price-tracking tool, and setting up email alerts to ensure you don’t miss rare discounts at Amazon and elsewhere. Leverage a price-tracking tool or deal aggregator The most effective way to find a truly great deal is to set up a price-tracking tool. We’ve included a few of our favorites below, many of which we use daily here at The Verge . Each can help you track deals at various retailers — including Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and Target — but they each do so differently and come with their own set of advantages / disadvantages. All of them are free to use, and once you’ve added the products you’re interested in keeping an eye on, you can rest easy knowing that you don’t need to take any action until it comes time to make a purchase. Just make sure you keep your email notifications on so you see the alerts as they come in. CamelCamelCamel CamelCamelCamel is arguably the most popular price-tracking tool at The Verge , and for good reason: it’s incredibly useful since it tracks the price of every product sold on Amazon and can send you alerts when an item falls to a customizable price threshold. Once a product reaches the desired price you’ve set (or lower), you’ll get an email about it. You can use the extension’s price graph to determine what price is likely to happen based on historical data, but it’s always a shot in the dark. To track prices and get alerts via email, you’ll need to create a free CamelCamelCamel account. Additionally, we suggest installing the site’s browser extension , The Camelizer, which works with Google Chrome, Safari, Mozilla Firefox, Opera, and Microsoft Edge. The handy tool lets you view pricing trends on a product-by-product basis and set your desired price without leaving Amazon. It’s fantastic, easy to use, and works in several countries, including the US, UK, Canada, Germany, Spain, France, Italy, and Australia. item.title: Here are the price-matching policies for Best Buy, Walmart, and others
item.description: Nothing is more frustrating than buying a new pair of headphones or an OLED TV, only to find out you could have gotten it cheaper somewhere else a few days or weeks later. That’s why, to keep customers happy and prevent them from shopping elsewhere, some retailers offer price-matching policies that promise to match a lower price found elsewhere. That kind of information comes in handy year-round, but it’s especially helpful during the weeks of deals leading up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday. Below are the price-matching policies for several major retailers. A few things to note: First, each retailer has its own set of rules and restrictions. We’ve summarized some of them here, but we recommend visiting the provided links and reading the policies carefully. Second, most retailers that serve as marketplaces for other sellers, including wholesale retailers like Costco, don’t offer protections, and many traditional stores won’t match their prices. Lastly, there are always exceptions to the rules. If you’re looking for a deal on a product and you know it’s available for a lower price elsewhere (or it was previously offered at the same retailer), it never hurts to call or chat with a customer service rep and ask if they’ll match the price. You have nothing to lose but time, and there’s always a chance they may find a loophole or make a special exception. Amazon Amazon doesn’t offer price matching. Full stop. You can contact customer support, but even if you’re an Amazon Prime customer, they likely won’t help. That said, the online retailer does offer a liberal return policy , meaning you can often return an item you purchased from Amazon if it’s available for less elsewhere (or at Amazon). Then, you can just repurchase the product wherever it’s cheapest. Target Target used to let shoppers price match identical items sold by select retailers, including Amazon, but no longer does so. Under its current policy, shoppers can only request a price adjustment if they find an identical qualifying item for less than they paid on Target.com, at their local Target store, or through an eligible Target Circle deal. Target will also price match Target Plus Partner (the retailer’s name for third-party sellers) items if the same Target Plus Partner on Target.com has it for less, or with a Target Circle deal. Price matches can be requested at the time of purchase or within 14 days after purchase. For the 2026 holiday season, Target has extended the aforementioned price-match window. If you purchase an eligible item between November 1st and December 24th, you can request a price adjustment if its price drops at Target during that period. The extended policy also applies to eligible Target Plus Partner purchases. To request a price match, you’ll need to show the online price or digital version of the ad and provide your original receipt or packing slip; screenshots and photos aren’t accepted. item.title: Here’s when the Black Friday sales start at Walmart, Target, and other retailers
item.description: Black Friday officially kicks off on November 27th, but if you plan to make that the only day you buy gifts this holiday season, you’re missing out. Several prominent retailers, including Best Buy and Walmart, are preparing to roll out their holiday discounts both in-store and online. Best Buy is even offering price protection through the holiday shopping season on select goods, so if you buy early and the same item drops in price, you can get the better deal retroactively. That being said, it’s important to know how every major retailer is handling the shopping event this year, whether you plan to take advantage of the slew of early holiday deals or hold off until the day after Thanksgiving. If you plan to spend some cash, here are the schedules and expectations for Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and all the major retailers we know of. Amazon Amazon has yet to announce its full Black Friday playbook, but the online retailer has dropped a few early deals in its so-called Holiday Shop , including steep discounts on Sony’s WH-1000XM6 headphones, the Google Pixel 11 Pro XL , and fitness trackers like the Fitbit Inspire 3 . Just be aware that Amazon does not offer price matching, so price “protection” for many Amazon shoppers means buying the item at the lower price point and returning the original — which, unfortunately, is pretty wasteful. Walmart Like in previous years, Walmart plans to roll out its Black Friday deals in three distinct waves. The first runs from November 12th through November 15th, starting online at 12:01AM ET and in stores at 6AM local time. Walmart Plus members will also get early access to some deals beginning at 12:01AM ET on November 12th, with the sale opening up to everyone at 12:01AM ET on November 13th. Walmart’s official Black Friday sale then kicks off at 12:01AM on Monday, November 23rd, with Walmart Plus members once again getting early access to select deals online. Whatever “hot Deal drops” remain will then be available to non-members at 12:01AM ET on November 24th. Walmart’s in-store Black Friday sale will then kick off at 6AM local time on November 27th. The retailer’s Cyber Monday sale, meanwhile, will kick off online at 12:01AM ET on November 30th and run through December 2nd. The retailer hasn’t shared many deal specifics yet, but did offer a sneak peek in a recent press release promising discounts across a range of categories, including toys, fashion, beauty, and home goods. Best Buy Best Buy officially kicked off its Black Friday promos on October 30th, with the retailer launching its first set of doorbuster deals on Halloween. Like last year, Best Buy will drop subsequent deals every Friday in the run-up to the holidays, and those who sign up for My Best Buy Plus or My Best Buy Total will also get up to $25 in bonus rewards during select doorbuster events. As for Best Buy’s main Black Friday event, the promos are slated to begin on November 19th and run for 10 days. The retailer will then hold its Cyber Sunday

item.title: Here are the shipping and return policies for all the big-name retailers
item.description: With the holidays quickly appro aching, everyone will soon be on the hunt for gifts and the fastest way to get them. Thankfully, many retailers offer generous shipping policies, with some even providing free two-day shipping or same-day delivery if you’re willing to pay a little extra. And just in case the gift you choose isn’t quite right, many retailers offer extended return policies so your giftee can get something more to their liking. For your convenience, we’ve compiled the current shipping and return policies for all the big-name retailers, from Amazon to Walmart. A few already have holiday policies in place, but we’ll be keeping tabs on them and updating our list accordingly. Hopefully, knowing more about how much leeway you have to make a return will help lessen that inevitable holiday angst (fingers crossed). Amazon Shipping : Same-day delivery is not available on Thanksgiving, Christmas, or New Year’s (it’s also limited on Black Friday). However, Prime members get free same-day delivery on qualifying orders in qualifying ZIP codes provided they meet the “minimum qualifying dollar threshold” ( which varies by location) of eligible items in their cart. One-Day and Two-Day Delivery with no minimum purchase amount required is also available to Prime members for qualifying products. Non-Prime buyers will find shipping options on the order page of each specific product. Returns : As part of its holiday promotional period, Amazon says most items purchased between November 1st and December 31st can be returned until January 31st, 2027. Apple products, however, must be returned by January 15th, 2027. Note that this policy applies to both Prime and non-Prime buyers. Apple Shipping : Apple has yet to provide details on its holiday shipping policy; however, last year, it offered free delivery of in-stock items that hadn’t been engraved by Christmas Eve if you ordered before 9PM ET on December 21st. Apple also offers free next-day or two-hour delivery from local stores in most metro areas for an additional fee, or you can opt to pick up purchases yourself by visiting your local Apple Store. Returns : Apple is offering an extended return period for online orders received between November 6th and December 25th, allowing you to return items until January 8th, 2027. Purchases made after December 25th are generally subject to the usual terms and conditions, and must be returned within 14 calendar days of your initial purchase date. Target Shipping : Target offers free two-day shipping on many orders if you spend $35 or more or use your Target Circle Card . Same-day delivery costs $9.99 per order, but it’s included with a Target Circle 360 membership ($10.99 a month / $99 a year). Your mileage may vary for same-day delivery availability based on the item and your location. Returns : Target offers an extended return policy for electronics and entertainment items purchased between November 1st and December 24th, allowing you to return them until January 24

item.title: The Verge’s guide to Black Friday 2026
item.description: Whether you’re hoping to finally upgrade your TV or simply get a head start on your holiday shopping, Black Friday still offers one of the best opportunities to save on the gadgets we prize most at The Verge . From wireless earbuds and smartwatches to robot vacuums and the latest gaming gear, retailers have already begun offering discounts across a wide swath of electronics, with more expected to drop as we approach the big day on November 27th. Love it or hate it, what once was a singular shopping day is now a drawn-out, monthlong affair. But with hundreds of thousands of items on sale, figuring out which deals are actually worth your time (and cold, hard cash) is easier said than done. Fortunately, to help you navigate another tariff-riddled shopping season , we’ve compiled all our Black Friday coverage in one place. Here, you’ll find the best deals we’ve spotted on our favorite gadgets, along with tips for making the most of your money . We’ll also be updating this page regularly in the weeks leading up to the holiday so you can keep up with the latest discounts as they arrive. item.title: Futuristic aircraft takes flight at NASA | Space photo of the day for Nov. 9, 2026
item.description: null The future of flight meets space exploration as a futuristic electric aircraft hovers beside Blue Origin's massive New Glenn rocket stage. (Image credit: Chelsea Gohd/Future) A futuristic single-person aircraft takes to the skies at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, with the upper stage of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket providing a dramatic backdrop. The unusual scene was captured during the MAX POWER event, which brought together innovators and emerging technologies at the iconic spaceflight facility. What is it? The photograph shows a single-person electric aircraft called Jetson ONE, developed by Jetson, a Swedish startup company working to bring personal flight to the skies. The compact rotorcraft uses multiple propellers to climb into the air, allowing it to take off and vertically without the need for a runway. The aircraft was performing flight demonstrations during the UP.Summit gathering, which formed part of the larger MAX POWER event at the Kennedy Space Center. During the demonstrations, the Jetson ONE demonstrated its ability to maneuver through the air and hover in place, giving spectators a close-up look at the technology in action. Jetson ONE demonstration at MAX POWER. (Image credit: Chelsea Gohd/Future) Why is it amazing? The photograph offers a fascinating glimpse at two very different approaches to flight. While Jetson is developing small electric aircraft designed for personal transportation, Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket is built to carry payloads far beyond Earth's atmosphere.

item.title: AFL Full Week Update: Tate Southisene, Briggs McKenzie continue to play well
item.description: SCOTTSDALE, AZ - SEPTEMBER 30: Briggs McKenzie #45 of the Atlanta Braves poses for a photo during the 2026 Arizona Fall League media day at Scottsdale Stadium on Wednesday, September 30, 2026 in Scottsdale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Tate Southisene 5-for-13, 3 RBI, 4 BB, 4 K, 3 SB The Tate shows continued last week as the Braves prospect got on-base nine times again last week. Even crazier, he continues to walk just as much as he strikes out. Then, you add in the fact that he’s also a menace on the bases and it’s hard to temper expectations for him. Tate also played in the AFL Fall Stars game where he went 0-for-2…but also drew a walk and scored a run. Tate has now played in 16 games and is hitting .321/.471/.396, going a perfect 7-for-7 on stolen bases. He has also walked (14) more than he has struck out (12). Isaiah Drake 3-for-9, 4 K, CS Isaiah appeared in just three games last week, getting on-base in two of the three games. After missing a big chunk of the season due to injury, Isaiah has adjusted to the league and put together high quality at-bats, making good contact with pitches in the zone. The result is Isaiah hitting .327/.386/.404 in 17 games, going 5-for-6 in the stolen base department. Owen Carey 2-for-10, 2 RBI, 2 BB, 2 K Owen appeared in three games last week, going 0-for-4 in his first game and then getting on-base four times in the final two games. After struggling with some injuries this year, Owen has now played in 16 games in the AFL and is slashing .283/.415/.396. Briggs McKenzie 4IP 3H 0R 2BB 6K Briggs looked very solid in his single start last week, striking out six across four innings. He did a great job of establishing his slider as his premium offering and using it in-zone very well, and generating whiffs from it. Also appears that Briggs is really working on the two-seam fastball to go with his four-seam. The slider, a pitch he focused on this season, now consistently looks above average. It will be interesting to see if Briggs brings back the curveball, or if the Braves have shelved it completely, but one thing remains 100% true – he knows how to generate spin. Tanner Bauman 1IP 1H 0R 1BB 0K After struggling early at the start of the AFL season, Tanner Bauman has done a good job of commanding his pitches – finding himself in-zone much more consistently. While the stuff hasn’t particularly been great, his execution has helped him find zeroes more consistently. Tyler LaPorte 1IP 1H 0R 1BB 2K Tyler appeared in one game, striking out two. He continues to show a strong arsenal, unique mechanics, and good command. A former position player who transitioned to pitching only a few years ago, Tyler could be a player to watch should the improved command show next season.

item.title: The Devils Have Improved Against The Metropolitan Division, But There’s Still Room For Growth
item.description: ELMONT, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 07: Jack Hughes #86 of the New Jersey Devils scores the winning goal in overtime against the New York Islanders at UBS Arena on November 07, 2026 in Elmont, New York. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Saturday, the New Jersey Devils fought back from a 4-2 deficit in the third period to notch a 5-4 overtime victory over the New York Islanders . This was a watershed moment for this club for a couple of reasons. First of all, the Islanders specifically have become one of the Devils’ boogeymen over the last few seasons. New York won all four meetings with New Jersey a season ago, including the lowest point of the 2025-26 campaign: The 9-0 loss on Long Island on January 6. They also beat the Devils, 6-0, in game number two of this season, meaning in their last two games on the island leading up to this one, New Jersey was getting outscored a bewildering 15-0 by the Isles. The last time the Devils actually won a game against the Islanders was exactly two years ago today: November 9, 2024. Second, in addition to the Islanders specifically, the entire Metropolitan Division as a whole was a titanic roadblock for the Devils last season. New Jersey went a pathetic 7-17-2 against divisional foes in 2025-26. Those struggles were one of the biggest reasons why they failed to qualify for the postseason. It’s still early, but the good news is that the Devils have experienced better results against the Metro this year. After Saturday’s win, New Jersey is now 3-2-0 in intra-division games in 2026-27. That’s not amazing, but clearly it’s worlds better than the mark they posted last year. And looking past the results, the Devils’ process has been much, much better against Metro competition as well. As we look for reasons why this season’s hot start is different from past seasons’ hot starts, this improved play against the Metropolitan Division should take a prominent role in our collective analyses. The Results So Far Here’s a quick rundown of New Jersey’s Metropolitan Division tilts thus far: October 1 vs. PHI: 3-2 OTW October 3 @ NYI: 6-0 L October 15 vs. NYR: 7-1 W October 17 @ WSH: 4-2 L October 7 @ NYI: 5-4 OTW They haven’t been able to string two wins against Metro squads together yet. They’ll have a chance to do so on Thursday when they host the Capitals in a big early-season matchup (with, presumably, Connor Hellebuyuck well-rested for that one! ). The two outliers there are obviously the first Islanders game, and the Rangers game. That October 3 game thankfully has been the only true disaster against the Metro so far. And the Devils certainly made up for that trainwreck by throttling the Rangers in their very next in-division contest. That loss against the Capitals was disappointing, but it’s hard to be too angry about a .600 points percentage. The Other Points Percentage But the Devils’ points percentage isn’t the only one that matters. It’s great that the Devils found a way to squeak out a pair of overtime

item.title: Luke Fox and Brooks Auger pitch in Fall Stars Weekend; the NL wins 7-4
item.description: SCOTTSDALE, AZ - NOVEMBER 08: Chase Harlan #11, Luke Fox #5 and Brooks Auger #36 of the National League Fall Stars pose for a photo in the dugout prior to the 2026 Arizona Fall League Fall Stars game between the American League Fall Stars and the National League Fall Stars at Salt River Fields at Talking Stick on Sunday, November 8, 2026 in Scottsdale, Arizona. (Photo by Jill Weisleder/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The National League beat the American League 7-4 in the Fall Stars Game, and while there were no Dodger hitters involved, with Chase Harlan absent from the game, two of their pitchers made an appearance. Luke Fox and Brooks Auger came within one strikeout (5) of equaling the AL’s total for the game (6) as the two pitching staffs displayed contrasting levels of stuff. Overall, the National League struck out three times as many hitters as the AL, 18 to 6 to be precise. Fox was one of two NL pitchers to be hit with a blown save; on multiple occasions, they surrendered the lead in the middle innings before opening a three-run lead in the eighth. Fox allowed one hit and an unearned run, striking out the side in the fifth. Auger followed in the seventh with a clean frame in what was then a tied game, punching out a couple to work around a walk. The National League used 11 pitchers in total, and each one of them secured at least one strikeout, while only four of 11 did that for the AL. Winner of the Home Run Derby—replacing Chase Harlan in the contest—Aaron Parker of the Blue Jays didn’t put the ball in play in three at-bats in the All-Star Game, twice striking out and once drawing a bases-loaded walk. On the NL side of things, Yerlin Confidan doubled and walked in two plate appearances, enough to be selected MVP of the game. Your 2026 Fall Stars Game MVP is Reds prospect Yerlin Confidan! pic.twitter.com/HPcO9oPNPJ — MLB's Arizona Fall League (@MLBazFallLeague) November 9, 2026

item.title: Oregon Ducks Football: Duck Tape Film Review Ohio State Buckeyes 2026
item.description: COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 7: Quarterback Luke Fahey #13 of the Ohio State Buckeyes is sacked by Nasir Wyatt #31 | Getty Images Author’s note: A full transcript of the video will be available by Monday evening. Here is a written account of my conclusions about the game for those who prefer to use the video only for play breakdowns. Oregon won this game because they were able to exploit Ohio State’s defense for big plays in the passing game, while the Buckeyes could not hit explosive plays to WR #4 Jeremiah Smith. Oregon’s offense was not efficient, but Ohio State was not consistent enough pressuring QB #8 Dylan Raiola who hit big plays when his receivers found holes in zone coverage. The Ducks’ defense shut down the short passing game the Buckeyes committed to with backup QB #13 Fahey in, and Ohio State’s run game was never a threat. The game definitively entered garbage time when the Ducks took a 38-14 lead early in the 4th quarter. This occurred at the end of Oregon’s 11th meaningful possession, whereas Ohio State only had 10 before they were too far behind to come back. The following players listed as “out” on the game day availability report are presumed lost for the season: QB #5 Dante Moore, DB #21 Aaron Flowers, ILB #23 Brayden Platt, and OL #56 Trent Ferguson. In addition both DL #55 Matthew Johnson and OL #74 Dave Iuli have been listed as out for several weeks in a row. For, presumably, different reasons WR #15 Messiah Hampton was also listed as out and will likely remain so indefinitely. Both starting running backs, RB #0 Jordon Davison and RB #6 Dierre Hill, exited last weeks game and didn’t return. Davison was out again this week, but Hill started and received the majority of the carries. In some good news, WR #3 Jeremiah McClellan was listed as a “Game Time Decision” after breaking his foot during warm ups before the Portland State game. I only spotted him once when he caught a short five yard pass in the second quarter. Oregon’s offense punished soft zone coverage with intermediate throws for explosive plays in the passing game against Ohio State’s defense. A couple well timed interior screens against Buckeye blitzes also resulted in explosive gains on touchdown drives. The offense benefited from favorable field position thanks to defense and special teams. Informed fans should not let the recent success mask lingering weaknesses with this offense: The offensive line is stable but still notably underperforming relative to what this unit should look like given the talent and experience in the room. QB #8 Dylan Raiola has once more proven he can be effective but he still has his limitations. There is some lingering irrationality in play calling (e.g., running too much between the tackles against this defensive structure and too many perimeter screens). item.title: Wingin’ It for ‘MNF’ with a Buffalo take on this classic Minnesota treat
item.description: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a themed recipe based on the Bills and their opponent. What could be sweeter than your favorite team on Monday Night Football ? This Minnesota-inspired cereal treat gives it a run for its money. Making this a bit more “Buffalo” was pretty easy, too. Scotcheerios The Vikings are a fun team for this series because they’re not a frequent opponent for the Bills, which means there’s still plenty to explore. When diving into Minnesota culture I came across scotcheroos, which is a type of cereal treat bar where the binding ingredient starts with corn syrup rather than marshmallow. The base recipe uses crispy rice cereal and straight corn syrup for the liquid sugar. I swap out the rice cereal and use the more “Buffalo” cereal of Honey Nut Cheerios, and then augment that flavor profile with a partial substitution on the corn syrup. Aside from that, this recipe is basically the same as this one from the Karo Syrup website , and I like to give credit where it’s due when my recipe doesn’t deviate all that much from someone else’s work. Scotcheerios Makes: About 20 treats Active time: 20 min Total time: 30 min Ingredients 1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips 1 cup butterscotch chips 3/4 cup light corn syrup (yes I used Karo and yes they should cut me an endorsement check) 1/4 cup honey 1 cup granulated sugar 1 cup creamy peanut butter 6 cups Honey Nut Cheerios (they also should cut me an endorsement check) Essentials: Greased 9×13 pan (use glass and thank me later), medium sauce pan, large glass bowl, high-sided sauté pan, large mixing bowl, measuring cups, rubber spatulas Partially fill the high-sided sauté pan with water; place the glass bowl in the pan (see below, and be careful of splashing). Add chocolate and butterscotch chips to the bowl; turn heat to MED (about 4 of 10 on my stove); continue with step 3 while allowing chips to melt. Add corn syrup, honey, and sugar to sauce pan on MED/HIGH (about 7 of 10 on my stove). Continuously stir syrup-sugar mixture until it begins to bubble; reduce heat to MED (4 of 10) and stir for another 2 min. Remove from heat and stir in peanut butter. Add cereal to large mixing bowl; quickly fold in syrup-peanut butter mixture. Carefully pour into greased pan and press to get even bars. Stir chocolate-butterscotch chips until smooth, then quickly spread on top of cereal mixture in pan. Cool for 45 min or longer; cut, and serve Wingin’ It tips If you’re not familiar with the melting technique I used, this is a cheap way to make a double boiler. item.title: Las Vegas’ AFC West slide continues with Broncos, Chiefs wins
item.description: (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 9 was brutal for the Las Vegas Raiders. Not only did they suffer a blowout loss to the San Francisco 49ers, but the Raiders also pretty much fell out of contention for the AFC West Championship. Not that Las Vegas had good odds of winning the division heading into the weekend, but the loss combined with the Denver Broncos’ and Kansas City Chiefs’ wins virtually puts an end to any slim hopes. On that note, let’s check in on the rest of the division, including the Los Angeles Chargers. Broncos vs. Panthers Score: 26-21 Broncos win Key Stats: QB Bo Nix: 25/37 (67.6%), 237 yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT RB Jonah Coleman: 17 carries, 57 yards (3.4 ypc), 1 TD, 4 catches, 31 yards WR Pat Bryant: 4 catches, 56 yards, 1 TD EDGE Nik Bonitto 2 tackles, 1 sack, 1 FF, 1 FR S Devon Key: 4 tackles, 1 INT This was a solid road win for the Broncos, as they scored on the game’s opening possession and led for three out of four quarters. Granted, Denver did get a scare in the third quarter, falling behind by a point. However, Key’s interception flipped the momentum back in the Broncos’ favor, leading to a two-score lead with about six minutes left. A late fumble by Coleman gave Denver a late scare, but the team had control of the game for the majority of the contest. Next week: Bye Chiefs vs. Jets Score: 35-12 Chiefs win Key Stats: QB Patrick Mahomes: 23/31 (74.2%), 242 yards, 2 TDs, 0 INTs RB Kenneth Walker III: 18 carries, 102 yards (5.7 ypc), 1 TD, 4 catches, 41 yards, 2 receiving TDs TE Travis Kelce: 4 catches, 72 yards, 1 rush, 1 yard, 1 rushing TD LB Nick Bolton: 12 tackles, 1 TFL, 1 FF EDGE George Karlaftis: 6 tackles, 2 sacks, 3 TFLs, 1 PD, 3 QB hits This was a pretty dominant performance where Kansas City outgained New York by more than 160 total yards. The Chiefs’ defense didn’t give up a touchdown in the first half and pitched a shutout in the second, while Walker turned in a three-touchdown performance while flirting with 150 yards from scrimmage. The only worry coming out of Kansas City was an injury to Mahomes’ throwing arm/elbow, but the quarterback came back into the game and isn’t believed to have a significant issue. He will undergo more testing on Monday, though. Next week: @ Falcons Pat Mahomes is on the sidelines after injuring his right arm on this play pic.twitter.com/rdOEkmr5uq — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 8, 2026 Chargers vs. Texans Score: 44-22 Chargers lose Key Stats: QB Justin Herbert: 13/23 (56.5%), 193 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT RB Omarion Hampton: 13 carries, 60 yards (4.6 ypc) WR Quentin Johnston: 1 catch, 58 yards, 1 TD LB Daiyan Henley: 10 tackles, 1 TFL, 1 INT S Tony Jefferson: 5 tackles, 0.5 sack This game was so bad that Herbert got benched. That might have been an effort to spare the quarterback, because Houston’s pass rush feasted on Los Angeles’ weak offensive line with eight sacks. item.title: Syracuse men’s basketball: what to watch vs Indiana
item.description: WASHINGTON, DC - MARCH 28: C.J. Fair #5 of the Syracuse Orange goes to the hoop against Cody Zeller #40 of the Indiana Hoosiers during the East Regional Round of the 2013 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament at Verizon Center on March 28, 2013 in Washington, DC. The Orange won 61-50. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Syracuse Orange (2-0) men’s basketball is on the road tonight to face the when the Indiana Hoosiers (2-0) at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. Tip-off is 6:30 and the game will air on FS1. Here’s what our staff is watching for: Dom: Offensive execution Against Central Connecticut, Syracuse had the ball constantly moving and everyone got involved in putting the ball in the basket. No player reached more than 18 points, but four got to double figures and eight had eight or more. Against a more talented defense the Hoosiers will put on the court, a lot of attention will be on what the offense looks like with the jump in competition. Max: Adjust to tougher competition These first two games have not been against teams that can be considered a competitive matchup, so Indiana is a big step up. Syracuse needs to be able to properly adjust to this jump in difficulty and maintain their skill level they’ve shown throughout the start of the season. The defense will be a big factor here, with the Hoosiers scoring over 90 points in both of their first two games. Kevin: Defend the paint It’s super early but Indiana has brought in 31 offensive rebounds in their first two games. I’m curious to see how a Syracuse team that is smaller at the center spot handles Aiden Sherell and Samet Yigitoglu especially on the offensive glass. The Orange guards will need to help out on the boards before looking to run. Since the perimeter defenders haven’t done a great job shutting off penetration so I’d expect to see more Dual in this one to help keep the Hoosiers on the outside. Szuba: Dual’s defense/guard matchups More on Kevin’s point, I’d expect to see Dual matched up with former Duke guard Darren Harris, who leads this Hoosier team in scoring with 15.0 points per game. I think Syracuse needs Dual’s defense in this game, yet the fourth-year college player hasn’t played to his potential on that end just yet. This game should tell us more about where Dual is at defensively and just how much time he earns over backup Ryan Moesch. Nonetheless, a 6-foot-5 guard on 6-foot-5 guard could be a fun matchup and so too could speed-on-speed with Moesch defending former Notre Dame guard Markus Burton. Sam: Physicality levers Syracuse wins the backcourt physicality battle with its starting group, but Indiana wins the frontcourt physicality battle with its two 7-footers. The Orange need to be aggressive defensively on the perimeter so as not to let the Hoosiers get the ball into the paint easily. Once they do, I’m a little worried about foul trouble for the bigs – first big boy test for Wilson. **********************************************************

item.title: Big Ten Football Power Rankings: See how far Ohio State tumbles
item.description: COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 7: Jamari Johnson #9 of the Oregon Ducks runs with the ball as Earl Little Jr. #1 of the Ohio State Buckeyes defends during the second quarter of the game at Ohio Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 10 of the Big Ten football season was highlighted by the return of the Oregon Ducks. While Dan Lanning’s squad likely isn’t back in the CFP picture, they ended Ohio State’s chances in an incredibly satisfying manner. Michigan also lost again, but we don’t need to talk about that. With just a few weeks left in the regular season, here are our latest Big Ten Power Rankings. 10. Minnesota Golden Gophers: 5-4, Lost to UCLA 20-34, LW: 9 Minnesota mostly bottled up UCLA’s offense, only giving up eight completed passes to Ty Dieffenbach. Unfortunately for the Golden Gophers, those eight passes went for 303 yards and three touchdowns. Minnesota has had an up-and-down year, and that looks likely to continue. 9. Illinois Fighting Illini: 6-3, Def. Nebraska 24-13, LW: 13 I had somewhat written off Bret Bielema and the Fighting Illini when they started the season 2-3 with losses to Duke, Ohio State and Purdue. However, Illinois has rattled off four wins in a row over Michigan State, Oregon, Maryland and Nebraska. I don’t think this team is good necessarily, but they warrant top-10 consideration in these rankings given how they’ve played in recent weeks. 8. Northwestern Wildcats: 6-3, Lost to Iowa 10-24, LW: 6 Northwestern being in the top-four was fun while it lasted. It’s now back to reality for the Wildcats, having lost consecutive games against Oregon and Iowa. item.title: Overreaction Monday: Sack Nation is back!
item.description: (Photo by Amy Kontras/Getty Images) | Getty Images After the Kansas City Chiefs’ win over the New York Jets in Week 9, we checked the comments on X to find the strongest reactions to the game. The question is: Are they overreactions or not? Thank god we won, but we need help. We don’t stand a chance against better teams right now. Thank god we won, but we need help. We don’t stand a chance against better teams right now. — Holly ✌🏻🏈 (@ChiefsNana) November 8, 2026 I agree the Chiefs need help, especially at receiver. But saying they don’t stand a chance against the better teams is a reach to me. They already beat Denver and were a couple yards away from sweeping them. If we’re calling Denver one of the best teams in the AFC, how can we sit here and act like the Chiefs can’t hang with those teams? Sack Nation is back! Sack nation is back! — 3rdnlong Chiefs' Poet / Songwriter (@Writer3rdnlong) November 8, 2026 The Chiefs got to Geno Smith five times, and Chris Jones, the leader of Sack Nation, had two of those sacks himself. That was good to see, but let’s be real about who they played. The Jets stink, and even after a five-sack game, the Chiefs are still near the bottom of the league in sacks. I need to see them do it against a better offense before I’m ready to say Sack Nation is back. We now need 2 wide receivers; Patrick Mahomes isn’t human. We now need 2 wide receivers, Patrick Mahomes isnt human. — Giulio Mancuso (@GiulioMan6) November 8, 2026 I’m with you on this one because as good as Patrick Mahomes is, the Chiefs have to get him some help. To me, the cleanest path is to trade for a receiver now, whether that’s Josh Downs or Brian Thomas Jr. If Tyreek Hill gets healthy enough to play at some point this season, I’d bring him back too. He already knows Andy Reid’s offense and has chemistry with Mahomes, so he should be able to slide right in. Release Butker and move on from Toub Release Butker and move on from Toub — Chris Sadler (@Csadler316) November 8, 2026 I’m with you on this one. Harrison Butker has fallen off a cliff, and it’s gotten to the point where even the kicks you used to pencil in feel like an adventure. Then you’ve got Dave Toub’s unit committing penalty after penalty, and at some point that falls on the coach. I’d be fine with the Chiefs moving on from both.

item.title: Selected Shots Monday: The Longhorn Chronicles
item.description: Mizzou wide receiver Naeshaun Montgomery (0) celebrates his touchdown against Texas on Saturday, Nov. 7 at Memorial Stadium in Columbia, Mo. | Margo Jenkins Another Mizzou Athletics sports season is upon us! While the last few years I’ve assigned this written piece to one of our talented photographers, I’m taking it over this year, and will be selecting my favorites of the week. Since I am not a photographer at heart, my analysis will be more surface level, but I’ll try my best! This week, Tiger Style returned, and we also were treated to women’s hoops, men’s hoops x2, volleyball x2 and football. Let’s get to it! Election Day Winner While I was working the polls— GO DEMOCRACY!! — Mizzou Men’s Hoops was tipping off its season with a black & gold tidal wave of their own with a 111-50 win over Cleveland State and former Mizzou staffer Rob Summers. Toni Bryant (15pts, 6 reb, 3 blocks), Mark Mitchell (11pts, 5 reb, 10 assists) and Kennard Davis, Jr. (19pts, 4 reb) led the first trifecta of the season. Fellow freshman Jason Crowe, Jr. had the highest +/- of the night, with a +51 with 23pts, 3 reb, and 2 assists. Tiger Style Dominates In what will be Brian Smith’s final season at the helm for Mizzou Wrestling, the Tigers dominated the Missouri Duals, losing just three duals across three matches against Central Methodist, Maryville and Central Missouri. Per Colin Simmons’ recap , despite the big day across the board for Mizzou’s 20 wrestlers that competed, head coach Brian Smith was dwelling on what needs to be fixed going forward. “We weren’t very good in a lot of situations, just guys not trusting their shape,” Smith said. “They figured it out at some point in the match, but they’ve got to have that trust from the beginning. But those are things we can work on. We had a leg a million times and didn’t get turns. We had turks and didn’t get turns, so those are the things my wheels are turning about, that we’ve got to be better in those positions.” Longhorns sweep While many (most?) of Mizzou Nation was tuning in to the Mizzou-SLU game, Dawn Sullivan & Co. welcomed in a nice-sized crowd of 3,600-plus at Hearnes and fought sooo hard against no. 13 Texas, though ultimately losing in three straight sets, 25-27, 13-25, and 23-25. The Rivalry Returns For the first time in 25 years, my two favorite teams — I grew up going to Billikens games — faced off against one another… and it was glorious, even if the black & gold lost this one. It was the difference between one connected team, SLU , who brings back 4/5 starters, vs. a team still trying to figure things out with two 5-star freshmen, six incoming transfers, and a late addition in Mark Mitchell. item.title: Brandon Lowe could fix the Orioles’ second base woes
item.description: DETROIT, MI - SEPTEMBER 26: Brandon Lowe #5 of the Pittsburgh Pirates throws to first during the game between the Pittsburgh Pirates and the Detroit Tigers at Comerica Park on Saturday, September 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Izzy Rincon/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The Orioles have a second base problem. A former University of Maryland standout might be just the guy to solve it. For the next two weeks, Camden Chat writers will be profiling a dozen players, either free agents or trade targets, that we’d like to see the O’s pursue this offseason. First up is an infield slugger with a local connection, free agent Brandon Lowe. To be clear, I’m not interested in Lowe solely because #HeATerp. I mean, it sure doesn’t hurt. But as a player, he checks a lot of boxes for the Birds. The two-time All-Star would bring some much-needed left-handed thump to the Orioles’ lineup. He’s a veteran of the AL East who has (mostly) crushed the Orioles’ division rivals. And he’d stabilize a position at which the Orioles were the worst in the league in 2026. Lowe (pronounced “Lau”) should be a familiar name for O’s fans. Those in the local area might have become aware of him during his College Park career in 2014-15, when he starred for a Maryland team that included five future big leaguers. Lowe also played one summer in the Cal Ripken Sr. Collegiate Baseball League as a 19-year-old. Even if you didn’t follow Lowe’s collegiate career, you surely know him from his near-decade as an O’s divisional opponent. After the Rays drafted him in the third round in 2015, he spent the first eight years of his MLB career with Tampa Bay from 2018-25 before a trade last offseason sent him to Pittsburgh. Aside from an abbreviated 2022 campaign, Lowe has been a well above-average hitter for every major league season, posting a career 123 OPS+ and averaging 4.2 bWAR per year. He’s had five seasons of 21+ homers and three seasons of 30 or more. Simply put, he’s one of the best hitting second basemen in the game. As a Ray, Lowe stepped up his game against division foes. He feasted on Orioles pitching (.857 OPS, 20 homers) and particularly torched the Red Sox (.994 OPS, 21 HRs) and Blue Jays (.918 OPS, 21 HRs) in more than 70 games against each opponent. He was less successful, though, against the Yankees, who held him to a .659 OPS. Lowe is coming off of his most productive year yet. In his debut season with the Pirates, he tallied 35 homers and 96 RBIs — both his highest totals since 2021 — and posted a career-best 5.3 bWAR. And it’s not just his offense that impressed. With the leather, Lowe pulled off an incredible turnaround after several years of subpar defensive marks. He registered 13 Defensive Runs Saved and 15 Outs Above Average this season after struggling to a -14 DRS and -14 OAA the season before. Could those numbers, especially on defense, have been a one-year mirage? It’s possible. At 32 years old, it’s unlikely that Lowe just suddenl

item.title: The 2026 National League Rookie of the Year Award presents an interesting philosophical debate
item.description: Sep 15, 2026; New York City, New York, USA; New York Mets right fielder Carson Benge (3) rounds the bases after hitting a home run during the third inning against the Baltimore Orioles at Citi Field. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The 2026 Rookie of the Year Award is one of the more fascinating award races this year (at least it is in the National League, since Kevin McGonigle should run away with the American League variant). New York Mets outfielder Carson Benge is one of the three finalists, alongside St. Louis Cardinals shortstop JJ Wetherholt, and Cincinnati Reds corner infielder (though mostly first baseman) Sal Stewart. Each of the three players have an interesting and varied case to bring home the hardware in what ended up being a hotly contested race (one of which that saw a few players snubbed as finalists, namely Mets starter Nolan McLean and Colorado Rockies first baseman TJ Rumfield, both of which would place easily in my personal top three). JJ Wetherholt represents the season-long interpretation of the award. He looked like the runaway favorite to win it for months, as his exceptional defense at second base (+25 DRS) and league-average offense (101 wRC+) gave him a huge head start, especially when Carson Benge was hitting like a pitcher for about a month or so. Wetherholt, despite only playing 139 games, led all National League rookies in fWAR with 4.6 — and trailed only Kevin McGonigle in fWAR among all rookies. He was a steady player for the Cardinals from the word go. He did miss a few weeks with wrist tendonitis, but he represents the safer vote. Sal Stewart represents a vote with an older school flair. Stewart was a mediocre defender (-2 DRS at first), and his wRC+ sat at 112, so it is fair to wonder how he ended up a finalist, especially when he finished with a rather tepid 2.0 fWAR, good for fifth among NL rookies, and 17th among all rookies. How he got here was his counting stats. Stewart hit 32 home runs, easily leading all NL rookies, and finishing only behind Munetaka Murakami and Kazuma Okamodo. His 112 RBI are twenty more than any other rookie, and were third in all of baseball. Those counting stats pop off the page, and his .263/.330/.457 slash line makes it look even better. Twenty or so years ago, Stewart wins this in a landslide and no one is batting an eye. Carson Benge represents a little from Column A and a little from Column B. His 4.3 fWAR is second among NL rookies and third among all rookies, pairing a solidly above average bat (118 wRC+) with solid defense (+1 DRS). He went 20/20 on the season, hitting exactly 20 home runs and swiping 22 bags. He also has the benefit of a narrative behind him. Benge was, for lack of a better term, horrific to start his rookie season, finishing April with a 48 wRC+. He turned it on from there, finishing May with a 128 wRC+. item.title: Jaguars vs. Titans odds: Opening lines for NFL Week 10 matchup
item.description: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - JANUARY 04: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars looks on against the Tennessee Titans during the first half at EverBank Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida.
