item.title: Monday Rockpile: Five things Rockies fans should watch for in the MLB GM meetings
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 23: MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred speaks with the media prior to game one of the 2026 World Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field on October 23, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Today, Major League Baseball’s General Manager Meetings begin in Las Vegas. Generally, the GM Meetings set the stage for later action, but with an all-but-assured lockout coming on December 1, this year may be different. At any rate, Colorado Rockies president of baseball operations Paul DePodesta will be there as will general manager Josh Byrnes, assistant general managers Ian Levin and Tommy Tanous, and director of baseball operations Amir Mamdani. They are scheduled to take questions from media on Tuesday afternoon, so look for us to follow up on that. At any rate, here are the big questions we have headed into this week’s meetings. Will teams, including the Rockies, begin an offseason frenzy of trades and signings, or will they wait until after the new CBA? Certainly, front offices will take different approaches to this question — whether they wish to makes deals in the known present or gamble on an undefined future. But given that the month is almost one-third over, if there’s going to be a busy November, it better get rolling. The GM Meetings should give fans a better sense of MLB’s mood. Will the Rockies make any trades? Three of the organization’s best moves last season were the result of trades: Brenan Bernardino , Jake McCarthy , and TJ Rumfield all came to the Rockies as the result of offseason trades. Moreover, last August’s trade deadline saw the Rockies making moves to shore up their pitching, and the early results were promising. Will we see more of this during the GM Meetings, and if so, which Rockies players might be trade candidates? Will the Rockies sign any free agents? In 2026, the Rockies had a mixed record when it came to signing free agents. Tomoyuki Sugano was a win; Willi Castro and José Quintana were fine, with the latter missing much of the season due to injury; and Michael Lorenzen was DFA’d in August. The question, then, becomes how deeply the Rockies will dive into the free agent pool. (Here’s MLB Trade Rumors’ annual “Top 50 free agents with predictions” for your bookmarking convenience.) The Rockies need starting pitching, and this year’s free agent class offers a wide range of talents and salaries. Based on what they learned in 2026, will the Rockies again make signings, and could that happen in the coming days? How will the front office answer questions about recent staffing changes? Last week, Christian Saez of DNVR reviewed recent communications he’d had with former Rockies pitching coach Alon Leichman and a member of the Rockies front office. The Rockies also announced hiring Ethan Katz as their new pitching coach. On Tuesday, Rockies media will be able to follow up with additional questions. We also know the Ro

item.title: Patriots vs. Packers snap counts: Christian Barmore in the spotlight ahead of NFL trade deadline
item.description: Even coming out of a blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers and dropping to 5-4 on the year, the New England Patriots are not necessarily in “seller” territory heading toward Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. That being said, one player has still been mentioned as a potential candidate to be moved over the past few weeks: defensive tackle Christian Barmore. Whether or not a trade will materialize remains to be seen, but Sunday’s game did little to clear the smoke emanating from that particular fire. Barmore, after all, played a season-low 26 of 61 defensive snaps for a playing time share of 39%. While the margin is not significant — he averaged 31 snaps and a 50% share over his first seven games — it, at the very least, creates more data points to fuel speculation over the next 24-plus hours. The other top-level DTs, after all, did not see such a drastic change relative to their normal usage. Milton Williams had a slightly lower playing time share than his season average up to that point, while Cory Durden was on the field a bit more. Does that mean a trade is imminent? No, it doesn’t. Playing time fluctuates based on a variety of factors including opponent, game script and physical fitness. In Barmore’s case, he did have some positive contributions by registering a sack and a stop on a 3rd-and-1 run. Of course, that probably still won’t stop the rumor mill from turning until 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday. Here is our full snap count report from the Patriots’ 45-27 loss . Offense Total snaps: 63 | Time on the field: 23:11 | * denotes starter C Jared Wilson* (63; 100%), RG Matt Pryor* (63; 100%), QB Drake Maye* (51; 81%), RT Morgan Moses* (51; 81%), WR Kyle Williams* (49; 78%), LT Will Campbell* (45; 71%), WR Mack Hollins* (43; 68%), WR DeMario Douglas (43; 68%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson* (38; 60%), TE Eli Raridon (36; 57%), WR Efton Chism III (32; 51%), LG Walter Rouse (32; 51%), TE Hunter Henry (31; 49%), LG Ben Brown* (31; 49%), LT/TE Caleb Lomu* (22; 35%), RB Lan Larison (14; 22%), TE Tanner Arkin* (14; 22%), QB Tommy DeVito (12; 19%), RT Marcus Bryant (12; 19%), RB Corey Kiner (11; 17%) The Patriots offense suffered even more injury losses against the Packers, with the most prominent being running back Rhamondre Stevenson departing in the fourth quarter — in what was effectively garbage time already — with a knee injury. With RB2 TreVeyon Henderson already out due to an illness, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison are next on the depth chart and likely to see increased opportunities should Stevenson show any signs of limitations heading into Week 10. Injuries also hit the offensive line once again. Left guard Ben Brown hurt his knee late in the second quarter and was unable to continue, with Walter Rouse entering the game in his place. Early in fourth quarter, left tackle Will Campbell also exited with a knee issue, even though he could have reentered the contest, per himself. Campbell’s departure also gave insight into the Patriots’ backup offensive line hierarchy

item.title: The WTA faces criticism after Jessica Pegula and Mirra Andreeva’s incident, ‘extremely disappointing’
item.description: Controversy has plagued the WTA Tour and its players over the past week. Ahead of the WTA Finals, Jessica Pegula and coach Mark Knowles were caught expressing some choice words about Mirra Andreeva and her coach, Conchita Martinez . “Conchita’s always been very nice to me, but I’ve lost a little respect for her because I’m like, this girl – I think she’s a nice girl – she’s just a diva,” Pegula said during her practice session, which was broadcast live on YouTube. “She needs to be humbled. She needs to be [inaudible] putting her in her place; [inaudible] stand up to her.” Jessica Pegula and Mirra Andreeva’s head-to-head record 2025 Qatar Open first round – Mirra Andreeva and Diana Shnaider defeated Jessica Pegula and Ashlyn Krueger, 4-6, 6-3, 10-7 2025 US Open quarter-finals – Jessica Pegula and Jack Draper defeated Mirra Andreeva and Daniil Medvedev, 4-1, 4-1 2026 Italian Open semi-finals – Mirra Andreeva and Diana Shnaider defeated Jessica Pegula and Storm Hunter, 6-1, 6-2 This development was wholly unfair on all parties involved: the comments made about Andreeva and Martinez were harsh, and Pegula’s right to some semblance of privacy during her practice session was also infringed upon . The WTA have since apologised for their error, admitting that they failed to properly inform WTA Finals participants of the presence of microphones around the practice courts. WTA Chairwoman Valerie Camillo has also apologised to Pegula , stating that the live-streaming of her private comments was ‘regrettable and unacceptable.’ Brad Gilbert, the former coach of Andre Agassi and Coco Gauff, has now reacted to the controversy. Brad Gilbert expresses his disappointment with the WTA after Jessica Pegula’s comments Andrea Petkovic, the former world number nine, began the discussion by expressing her disappointment, arguing that Pegula and Knowles’ private conversation should have never seen the light of day. “It’s obviously extremely disappointing,” Gilbert, speaking on the Big T Podcast, then added. “I think as a player, you know on the Centre Court there is a microphone and you got to always be careful. But on a side practice court, you’re not thinking about it. “I think she did the right thing going up to Mirra and trying to iron things out. Obviously Coco got brought into it because she was talking about her in light, that if she did things like Coco, she would do… none of that matters. “But, to me, it was very disappointing of the WTA to not let the players know that. Then this thing would have never happened. But obviously, it’s out there now.” “We talked about it a little bit with the Jannik Sinner situation. My argument – I think I’m the only one arguing that – but I’m saying that sickness, injury, illness, those are private things,” Petkovic added. “In a normal environment, you are not supposed to disclose whether you are sick or injured. So we don’t have the right to know about Jannik Sinner’s injury if he doesn’t want to tell us, that was my chance, and

item.title: The Good, The Bad and The Ugly: LSU vs. Alabama
item.description: AUBURN, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 24: Head coach Lane Kiffin of the LSU Tigers looks on during the first half of an NCAA football game against the Auburn Tigers at Jordan Hare Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Auburn, Alabama. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) | Getty Images The difference a bye week makes. It seems like the bye week set LSU back. The progress the team was making leading up to the Auburn game was all thrown away in one game against Alabama. This was the first game in which LSU faced a ranked opponent, got handled, and suffered a lopsided defeat. Here are the good, the bad, and the ugly from the Alabama game. The Good: In contrast to what some of the LSU fan base may believe, the LSU defense was actually good in this game as an entire unit. Alabama came into this game averaging 342 yards per game on the road. On Saturday, LSU held the Tide to just 285 total yards. Alabama normally averages 129 rushing yards and 213 passing yards on the road, and LSU held the Tide below both averages, allowing only 206 yards through the air and 79 yards on the ground. LSU was also able to record two sacks on Keelon Russell. But even better than the defense was Jackson Harris, who continued to showcase exactly why he is one of the best receivers in the SEC. Harris finished the game with 166 receiving yards on 11 receptions. He was the most consistent threat LSU had offensively, along with Trey’Dez Green. Green finished with 10 catches for 85 yards on 11 targets. I would like to see both players get more opportunities in the red zone to potentially help address those issues. The Bad: The red zone and offensive line continue to show up as glaring weaknesses for this team. LSU had a clear objective to beat Alabama: run the football and convert in the red zone. LSU finished the game with just 77 rushing yards, and Dilin Jones accounted for 57 of them, with 48 coming after first contact. The offensive line wasn’t getting any push and, for the first time in several weeks, gave up multiple sacks. Leavitt did run himself into a couple of them, but there were also missed blocking assignments, unblocked pressures, and pass rushers who disrupted the timing of routes in key situations. The play at the line of scrimmage also impacts how the offense can perform in the red zone. If a team gets inside the 20-yard line and cannot run the ball consistently, it allows the defense to dictate how it wants to play because there isn’t much field left to defend. The defense can treat the offense as one-dimensional, become more aggressive, and disguise blitz packages and coverages. These issues seemed like they were getting corrected, and with the return of Trey’Dez Green last week, it appeared LSU was turning the corner and progressing in the right direction offensively at the right time. item.title: Idaho to the Playoffs? There’s a Chance
item.description: SALT LAKE CITY, UTAH - SEPTEMBER 3: Joshua Wood #3 of the Idaho Vandals instructs team before the game against the Utah Utes at Rice-Eccles Stadium on September 3, 2026 in Salt Lake City, Utah. (Photo by Bryan Byerly/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images On Saturday evening Idaho smashed Eastern Washington 62-31 picking up not only their fifth win of the season but their fifth win in six games, extending one of the hottest streaks in the FCS. Once left for dead at 0-4, the Vandals are suddenly 5-5 with two weeks to play and they’ve built quite a resume along the way. Could Thomas Ford’s team actually come all the way back and nab a playoff spot if they end up running the table? It would be hard to argue against them. One could hardly fault Idaho for some of the losses it suffered in the non-conference portion of its 2026 slate. The Vandals fell to FBS Utah (who is currently 9-0 and ranked #2 in the AP Polls), a Lamar team that’s headed to the playoffs and just pulled off one of the upsets of the weekend over Stephen F. Austin, and an Abilene Christian squad that has been to the postseason two years in a row. Save for an rough last-second defeat at the hands of Cal Poly back in Week 0, the losses during the first month of the year were not ones that were necessarily catastrophic. The wins, meanwhile, are about as good as anyone in the Big Sky has right now. The Vandals got themselves on the map with their miraculous last-second win over defending national champion and then-#1 Montana State on national TV to kick off October. It was a herculean effort that kicked off the run that they’re on right now. Two weeks after that big win, they rolled into Missoula and slayed the other Montana giant with a 42-35 triumph over the Griz. They haven’t lost since. It sets up two massive games against UC Davis and rival Idaho State over the next two weeks; a pair of games that Idaho absolutely needs to win if it wants to be in consideration for one of those last few playoff spots. How realistic is it, though, that the committee would actually grant them one if that scenario were to come to pass? In that case, the Vandals would be 7-5 and 7-2 in conference play. It is not unheard of for a five-loss team to qualify for the playoffs as an at-large. In 2021 Northern Iowa got the nod at 6-5 and that was with closing their season with two losses in their final three games. Morgan State got in with a similar record in 2014 as did Indiana State that same year. There is a path for Idaho to do the same. If they were to get it done, too, the Vandals would be a team that no one would want to see in the postseason. They would be riding in with six consecutive wins on the backs of an deadly offense. Led by dynamic signal caller Joshua Wood, Idaho has gotten the better of some of the best defenses the Big Sky has to offer this year. The unit is putting up 437.6 yards and 33.9 points per game. Wood has thrown for 2,807 yards and run for another 54

item.title: Shenendehowa girls' and Shaker boys' soccer teams lead Section 2's massive state semifinal contingent
item.description: Shenendehowa junior Lily Iacovetti, left, and junior Lillyann Palmer celebrate a goal during the state quarterfinals against Cicero-North Syracuse on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, at Niskayuna High School in Niskayuna, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) With three goals already in her pocket and 25 minutes left in Saturday's Class AAA regional final, Shenendehowa forward Lillyann Palmer was given a new job. Stop the other team from scoring. Coach Holli Mulholland moved Palmer from winger to outside back to protect a lead rather than build one and the Mustangs held on to beat Cicero-North Syracuse 5-1 in steady, driving rain at Niskayuna High School. The win earned Shenendehowa its first NYSPHSAA final four trip since 2023 and put the Mustangs two wins away from their first state title since 2004. Cicero-North Syracuse spent the early portion of the game trying to contain junior Brittany Tetlack, Shen's top scorer. That left room for Palmer, a junior in her first year with the program after transferring from Colonie, who scored twice midway through the first half. "We say this every week," Mulholland said. "When you shut one down, the other one comes alive." The Northstars cut Shenendehowa's lead to 2-1 late in the first half, but senior Annika Aley restored the two-goal cushion before the break. Palmer's third goal came in the second half, and Tetlack added the final goal in the closing minutes. Palmer was quick to credit her teammates. "It takes the whole team," she said, "especially the bench and the energy that we have." For the returners, the win carried a year's weight. Shen's season ended last fall in overtime against Saratoga Springs in the Section 2 final. "These guys recognized the opportunity and punched their ticket today," Mulholland said. "These guys are tight. They're connected. They're having a good time doing what we do." Ten Section 2 teams are headed to the state semifinals: four girls' teams (Shenendehowa, Bethlehem, Schuylerville and Stillwater) and six boys' teams (Shaker, Bethlehem, Averill Park, Schuylerville, Greenville and Northville). Stillwater keeps its repeat bid alive Defending girls' Class C champion Stillwater beat North Salem 4-0, with Kamryn VanPelt scoring two goals and Brooke Hodgson adding a goal and an assist. It's Stillwater's third straight trip to the final four. Section 2 sweeps boys' regionals Section 2 will have a boys' team in the semifinals in all six classes, and five of them got there by a single goal. Class AAA: Sami Terra scored in the first half, and goalkeeper Alex Cross made a save in the final seconds to preserve Shaker's 1-0 win over Cicero-North Syracuse. Class AA: Bethlehem beat No. 1 Watertown 2-0, behind two goals from Ayaz Sajid. Those were Watertown's only goals allowed all postseason. Class A: Averill Park held off Peru 2-1 on goals from Evan LaPier and Gabriel Mussett. Class B: Colden Harrison's goal with 12 minutes left gave the Schuylerville boys a 1-0 win over Saranac.

item.title: OFFICIAL: Raúl becomes Oviedo’s coach
item.description: Real Madrid legend Raúl González has signed for Oviedo and will be their coach until the summer of 2028, the club announced on their website. Per Realoviedo.es Real Oviedo has reached an agreement to appoint Raúl González Blanco as the new head coach of its first team until June 2028. Mr. González Blanco, 49, was born on June 27, 1977, in Madrid. The new Oviedo coach spent the majority of his playing career with Real Madrid, where he became a legend after more than 15 years in the club’s white jersey. After stints with Schalke 04, Al-Sadd Sports Club and the New York Cosmos, Mr. González Blanco retired as a player in 2015. As a coach, the Madrid native began his career in Real Madrid’s youth system, joining in 2018 to coach the Cadete B and Juvenil B teams. Subsequently, in 2020, he coached the Juvenil A team, winning the UEFA Youth League. Following this success, he led Real Madrid Castilla for six seasons. Now, Mr. González Blanco takes the helm of Real Oviedo’s first team and will manage his inaugural match as the new “azul” coach this Saturday against Girona FC at the Carlos Tartiere stadium. The new Real Oviedo coach will not issue statements until his official presentation. This will be Raúl’s first chance to coach a team in professional football, given that Castilla has always been considered a team for Real Madrid’s prospects to develop.

item.title: Jordon Hudson files lawsuit over viral Bill Belichick Ring cam video
item.description: Jordon Hudson has made more headlines over the past couple of years than her now-alleged ex-boyfriend, Bill Belichick . The North Carolina head football coach dated Hudson for two years, but they allegedly broke up in late 2025. Belichick hasn’t been too vocal about their relationship, but she allegedly had a ton of influence over his life. Many have discussed their age gap: Belichick is 74, while Hudson is 25. The eight-time Super Bowl champ was caught on a leaked Ring camera video leaving a rental house shirtless in Winthrop. It sparked questions about Belichick and what the former New England Patriots ‘ head coach was up to. Well, Hudson is taking legal action now. MORE: Bill Belichick bristles at Jordon Hudson question during press conference Why is Jordon Hudson filing a lawsuit? item.title: Xavi believes Barcelona fans undervalue Frenkie de Jong
item.description: Xavi believes Barcelona fans undervalue Frenkie de Jong It is fair to say that Xavi knows a thing or two about playing in midfield for Barcelona . The World Cup winner has since hung up his boots and taken charge of the Netherlands , and as a result, has taken a Barcelona midfielder under his wings. Speaking to the Spanish media ahead of the upcoming international break, Xavi has been casting his opinion on Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong. Xavi believes that the Barcelona fanbase should do more to appreciate what de Jong brings to the side. The former Champions League winner said ‘I think he is undervalued, but not by the coaches and his teammates. You have to listen to the people who are with him every day, because if you ask who the best midfielder is, they say Frenkie ‘. De Jong left Ajax to join Barcelona back in 2019. Now at the age of 29, de Jong has amassed over 300 appearances for Barcelona, with 20 goals scored in that time. He has won La Liga on three occasions and two Copa del Reys. Despite this success, Xavi believes that Barcelona fans expect more from de Jong, even though he has, in Xavi’s mind, been one of the best players at Barcelona. The current Dutch national team coach said ‘ De Jong is sometimes frustrated because he feels that Barcelona fans do not give him the recognition he deserves. They criticize him because he has not become the leader they dreamed of when he arrived from Ajax ‘. De Jong had to fill in at right-back for Barcelona against Atletico Madrid this weekend, something he is unlikely to do with the Dutch national team over the next week. Xavi and co face tough fixtures against Greece and Germany over the next few days. GBeNeFN | Ben Jackson

item.title: Insider wants to talk about killer problem, and it’s not just Buccaneers’ Baker Mayfield
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Insider wants to talk about killer problem, and it’s not just Buccaneers’ Baker Mayfield appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Buccaneers ’ passing attack faces growing scrutiny after Sunday’s 27-24 loss to the Chicago Bears. Baker Mayfield struggled, but the Buccaneers also failed to capitalize on several opportunities because of mistakes from their receiving corps. Tampa Bay forced five turnovers but still couldn’t secure the victory. The offense struggled to sustain drives despite receiving numerous chances from its defense. Buccaneers insider Rick Stroud questioned the quality of Tampa Bay’s wide receivers following the disappointing result. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Time to talk about the quality of the Bucs WRs,” Stroud wrote. He highlighted Ted Hurst’s limited involvement after the rookie dropped his only target. Hurst played just one offensive snap, according to Stroud, before Tampa Bay benched him. Emeka Egbuka also struggled to make a significant impact. He caught three of five targets for 38 yards after returning from a foot injury. Meanwhile, Tez Johnson finished with 76 receiving yards on two catches. However, a 57-yard reception accounted for most of his production . Stroud also suggested Johnson dropped two catchable passes, further illustrating the offense’s problems with execution. Mayfield wasn’t blameless either. His two interceptions included a costly pick-six that helped Chicago maintain its advantage. Still, the receiving struggles raise broader questions about Tampa Bay’s offensive consistency. The Buccaneers previously entered the season evaluating their receiving depth following major roster changes. The offense needs more reliable contributions from its pass catchers, especially during critical downs. Tampa Bay now enters its bye week with several issues to address. Improving receiver execution could prove just as important as correcting Mayfield’s mistake. item.title: FG considers assessment tests for Nigerians with foreign degrees before NYSC
item.description: The Federal Government is considering the introduction of assessment test for Nigerians who obtain degrees from foreign institutions, particularly in African countries. Dr Folake Olatunji-David, Acting Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Education, disclosed this at the 37th meeting of the National Standing Committee (NSC) on Evaluation of Foreign Qualifications in Abuja on Monday. Olatunji-David said the assessment test was necessary before their qualifications would be evaluated for mobilisation into the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC). She said the proposal was aimed at ensuring that foreign qualifications presented by Nigerians reflected genuine learning achievements and met the required academic standards. She explained that the measure was particularly important given the increasing number of Nigerians studying in foreign higher institutions, especially in West Africa. “We must ensure that the standard of education in Nigeria is not lowered by allowing all manner of foreign qualifications that are not recognised to be paraded by Nigerians without the corresponding learning achievement. “In as much as we want to encourage global socialisation, education, and the rest of them because the world is a global village now, but we want to maintain standard. “We want to ensure that, yes, for every certificate given, they are earned, and they can produce people that can contribute positively to our national development. “I therefore invite this committee once again to consider, if necessary, an assessment test before such graduates are evaluated for NYSC,” she said. Olatunji-David described the committee as central to efforts to safeguard the integrity of Nigeria’s education system by ensuring that only genuine and duly accredited foreign qualifications were recognised. She expressed concern over the rising cases of forgery of Nigerian and foreign degree certificates, saying the ministry was taking steps to address the menace. The acting permanent secretary commended members of the committee for decisions reached at their previous meeting, describing them as important steps towards improving the evaluation and accreditation of foreign qualifications. She said the ministry had recorded progress in confirming the accreditation status of foreign institutions, issuing clearance letters for NYSC mobilisation, authenticating certificates and issuing no-objection letters. According to her, the ministry also issues eligibility and proficiency letters to Nigerians travelling abroad for employment or further studies. “Since the beginning of this year, the evaluation of foreign certificates and authentication of Nigerian certificates have been automated and digitalised, making the process seamless. “The fees accruing are remitted into government accounts, thereby increasing the ministry’s revenue generation,” Olatunji-David said. item.title: ‘I’m happy with where we are’: Dana White talks about Zuffa’s performance in 2026
item.description: Dana White appeared for a post-fight presser over the weekend and fielded media questions, many of which were about Zuffa’s position in the sport. White would assert that he’s very comfortable with the job his company has been doing thus far, and that he’s looking forward to growing even bigger and better in the future. Here are some excerpts of what he had to say below. White on how he’d describe Zuffa’s first year in the boxing business “We have 25 deals in 95 countries right now. One of the big things I always tell fighters is obviously making money and all these things are important when you’re a professional athlete, but how many people see the great things that you accomplish in your career, too… “I’m happy with where we are in just under a year. Really happy. We’re ahead of where I thought we might be.” On whether Zuffa has changed their position on working with sanctioning bodies “We’re sort of dealing with that on a case by case basis and if we can work it out, we’d like to for the fighters. If we can’t, then we won’t.” On whether he can get along with Eddie Hearn to promote Fury vs AJ “Yeah, I don’t have a problem with Eddie Hearn. When’s the last time you guys have heard me talk about Eddie Hearn? I mean, I don’t have a problem with Eddie Hearn…You’re asking me about Eddie Hearn right now.” On how he’d rate Zuffa’s year “I’m happy with our first year. And for me, I’ve actually had a good time this year. I’ve had a good time, you know, working in the sport, on the sport, with the team that I’ve built. We’ve had a good time and we’re happy with where we’re at just a few months into our first year.” On if he anticipates having more US cards in the coming year “I think more cards, period. Everywhere. I think you’ll see us just like the UFC, taking the fights everywhere, all over the world, not just the US and the UK.” On the split with Shakur Stevenson “Well, I don’t think we let Shakur go without a fight. I mean, we worked together and we were on a call one day and I said ‘maybe it’s just better if we all go our separate ways’ and everybody agreed. “It just didn’t work out. You win some, you lose some.” On how he plans to take over boxing when the biggest names in the sport are aligned with other promoters “Well, we’re like eight or nine months into this thing. We’ll see how it all plays out.” On whether he feels he needs to make it up to the British public for trying to take Fury vs AJ outside of the UK “[Long pause]…No. I think that obviously when tickets went on sale, it killed it. It did incredibly well and I think it would’ve done well at Madison Square Garden, too.” On who is deciding the undercard of Fury vs AJ “Well, we made some fights on the undercard…I’m not going to get into this stuff. I’ll see you in Cardiff, though.”

item.title: MLB awards predictions: MVP, Cy Young, & other award winners for 2026 season
item.description: The 2026 MLB season saw incredible individual performances, and the league will hand out the official awards this week. Several players put together exceptional campaigns, while a pair of managers helped their clubs exceed expectations. From Junior Caminero’s power production to Jacob Misiorowski’s dominance on the mound, here are the predictions for MVP, Cy Young, Manager of the Year, and Rookie of the Year in both leagues. MORE: Predicting MLB free agent landing spots in 2026-27 offseason MVP Oct 19, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Rays third baseman Junior Caminero (13) hits a single during the second inning against the Cleveland Guardians at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) AL MVP: Junior Caminero, Tampa Bay Rays Caminero gets the American League MVP prediction after another tremendous power season. The Rays third baseman finished with a .276 batting average, 42 home runs, 101 RBI, and an .884 OPS across 162 games. He also finished among the AL leaders in home runs and total bases. At just 22 years old, Caminero became one of the youngest players in MLB history to record multiple 40-home-run seasons. His combination of production and consistency makes him a strong choice for the award. NL MVP: Pete Crow-Armstrong, Chicago Cubs Crow-Armstrong is the pick after delivering one of the most complete seasons in baseball. He finished with a .280/.372/.570 slash line, 45 home runs, 107 RBI and 41 stolen bases. His 9.8 Baseball-Reference WAR led the majors, and his elite defense in center field added even more value. Crow-Armstrong has a compelling case to take home the National League MVP. Cy Young Sep 29, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees pitcher Cam Schlittler (31) pitches against the Boston Red Sox during the first inning during game one of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) AL Cy Young: Cam Schlittler, New York Yankees Schlittler is the selection after putting together a dominant season in the Yankees’ rotation. He finished with a 14-6 record, 1.95 ERA, 0.91 WHIP and 193 2/3 innings pitched. He also averaged 11 strikeouts per nine innings and accumulated 7.0 Baseball-Reference WAR. His ability to limit baserunners while consistently missing bats makes him a deserving choice for the American League’s top pitching honor. NL Cy Young: Jacob Misiorowski, Milwaukee Brewers Misiorowski gets the National League prediction after an outstanding season that included a 15-5 record, 1.86 ERA and 0.80 WHIP across 174.2 innings. He averaged 13.1 strikeouts per nine innings and finished with 6.1 Baseball-Reference WAR. His 1.86 ERA and ability to overpower opposing hitters helped separate him from the rest of the National League pitching field. item.title: Texans Week 9 snap counts: How much did WR Tank Dell play in win over L.A. Chargers?
item.description: Just like that, the Houston Texans are back in the conversation for postseason chatter. In his return back to Los Angeles, C.J. Stroud threw for a season-high 384 yards and tied his career high in touchdown passes with five as the Texans rolled past the Los Angeles Chargers in a 44-22 victory at SoFi Stadium. Despite a slow offensive start, Houston found a rhythm in the second quarter and never looked back. Stroud, who wanted to see an uptick in consistency after Week 7's overtime loss to the New York Giants , threw an early pick on a pass that was batted at the line of scrimmage. He missed Nico Collins on a third-down conversion and overthrew Marvin Harrison Jr. in the second quarter. Outside of that, the former No. 2 overall pick looked like the quarterback that was promised back when drafted out of Ohio State in 2023. He connected with four different receivers, including twice with Kayshon Boutte for touchdown passes. Six passes went for gains of over 20-plus yards and were recorded as explosives. The Texans punted with less than two minutes in the second quarter. Kai Kroeger would only take the field one more time for the rest of the afternoon. For as good as Stroud was, the Texans' defense delivered a much-needed, jolt-worthy performance while attacking Justin Herbert. The Chargers' quarterback, who entered Sunday as the second-most-hit passer through eight weeks, took over at No. 1 as Houston's defense recorded a season-high eight sacks, including two each by Sheldon Rankins and Jadeveon Clowney. Entering the third quarter, Los Angeles tried to get something moving in the passing game, but an interception by Derek Stingley Jr. stopped a chance for a scoring drive. On the flip side, Stroud found Nico Collins, who made an impressive one-handed catch for a 13-yard touchdown grab, only extending Houston's lead by 26. But perhaps the best moment of the day came with Tank Dell's arrival back on the field. After missing nearly two seasons with a severe leg injury suffered in 2024, Dell didn't seem to miss a beat, hauling in four passes for 105 yards, including a 63-yard touchdown reception in the second quarter. Below is a breakdown of the playing time from Sunday's win, including some separation at wide receiver, running back, tight end and a deeper rotation at linebacker. Offense Before the bye week, Dell was on a snap count. He was only expected to have about 12-16 snaps per contest. On Sunday, he recorded 33 snaps, which correlates to roughly 47% of all plays. Even if the ball wasn't going to him, he still showed that the knee could hold up in coverage. New wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. was limited in his receptions, but it's become clear that the Texans plan on giving him a chance to prove his potential and a future No. 2 weapon opposite Nico Collins and Dell. He recorded 32 snaps, so roughly, he was out there for 46% of all plays. As for the offensive line, no changes whatsoever, though Blake Fisher only saw action in the jumbo package o

item.title: NFL Insiders Reveal What Detroit Lions Are Seeking Before Trade Deadline
item.description: The Detroit Lions are running out of time to make a move before the 2026 NFL trade deadline, and multiple national insiders believe general manager Brad Holmes is looking for help on defense. With Tuesday’s deadline rapidly approaching, Detroit has emerged as a team worth monitoring. The biggest priority appears to be cornerback, a position that has generated plenty of discussion throughout the season. But that might not be the only area Holmes is evaluating as the Lions prepare for the second half of their schedule. According to reporting from ESPN’s Dan Graziano, Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer, and The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones, the Lions have been exploring opportunities to strengthen their secondary. Linebacker is another potential area of interest following the frightening injury to Jack Campbell. And with the trade deadline set for Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET , Holmes has a limited window to improve a roster that is now 6-2 following Sunday’s 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins. The question is whether Detroit will find the right opportunity to make a meaningful upgrade. Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes takes a selfie with fans at warmup ahead of the game between Arizona Cardinals and Detroit Lions at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Multiple NFL Insiders Point to Detroit’s Biggest Need The Lions’ search for cornerback help has become one of the more consistent storylines surrounding this year’s trade deadline. Several national reporters have identified Detroit as a team that could be active in the market for another defensive back. In his November 4 reporting, ESPN insider Dan Graziano revealed that both Detroit and the Chicago Bears have been checking on potentially available cornerbacks. That report provided another indication that Holmes is evaluating his options rather than simply standing pat with his current roster. Meanwhile, Breer offered a similar assessment while discussing Detroit’s situation. He indicated that the Lions have been looking around the league for potential help in the secondary. “I would say right now they are looking for secondary help and they have been looking around for corners,” Breer explained, as documented in a November 3 Lions Wire report . More recently, Jones added another intriguing possibility to the conversation. In his November 7 reporting, Jones indicated that Detroit and Chicago would both like to add cornerback help at the right price. Jones also suggested Denver as a team that could attract interest because of its depth at the position. That doesn’t mean Detroit has entered negotiations with the Broncos, but it provides another potential direction for Holmes as the deadline approaches. And as previously reported , the Lions were already involved in trade discussions earlier this season for Joey Porter Jr. before he landed with the Dallas Cowboys. item.title: Tennessee opens as a small favorite at Texas A&M
item.description: Aggies Quarterback Marcel Reed 10, The LSU Tigers take on the Texas A&M Aggies. September 19, 2026; Baton Rouge, LA, USA; at Tiger Stadium. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Tennessee completed the first of their final four objectives in the 2026 season on Saturday night, beating Kentucky 34-6. The Volunteers ran for 240 yards against the No. 6 Wildcats while holding them to just six points on the night. It was a statement win for Tennessee, but the challenges keep coming this weekend. Tennessee now heads to Texas A&M, tasked with taking on Kyle Field. The Volunteers dropped their last road test to South Carolina after melting down in the closing minutes. Tennessee also had a shaky showing at Arkansas a couple of weeks prior. Texas A&M may be in the midst of a disappointing season, but they haven’t stopped fighting. The Aggies took Alabama to the fourth quarter in Tuscaloosa, and nearly knocked of South Carolina last weekend in Columbia. Texas A&M now returns home to College Station for the first time in three weeks, set to greet Tennessee with a blackout. Almost eerily similar to a few weeks ago when the South Carolina line came out, Tennessee has opened as a 2.5 point favorite over Texas A&M, according to Fanduel Sportsbook . Unlike the South Carolina line, this spread held across markets through Sunday night and into Monday morning. The total sits at just 42.5 points. Texas A&M, despite the effort, is 4-5 on the year. The Aggies were a preseason top ten team, appearing to return a talented defense and a veteran quarterback in Marcel Reed. To be blunt, it hasn’t gone well for the Texas A&M offense or Reed. The Nashville native has thrown for just over 1,600 yards on the season while tossing eight interceptions. He’s added 206 yards on the ground. Tennessee’s aggressive defense and outstanding pass rush certainly will have an opportunity to get after Reed and force some more of those mistakes on Saturday. The Volunteers have been to College Station just one time, coming ten years ago. It was an overtime thriller, but Tennessee ultimately fell 45-38. Tennessee won the last meeting against the Aggies in Knoxville back in 2023. Saturday will serve as the sixth meeting all time between the two schools. Kickoff is set for 3 p.m. ET in College Station. ESPN will have the call.

item.title: NFL Mock Draft 2027: Eagles land Jeremiah Smith
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 31: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes looks on against the USC Trojans at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on October 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles’ playoffs odds are bordering on an impossibility at this point. Barring some epic collapses from Philly’s NFC East rivals (possible) combined with the greatest turnaround you’ve ever seen from the Eagles offense (absolute fantasy), Howie Roseman should be looking ahead to the offseason. As it currently stands, the Eagles hold the fifth overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. I would be shocked if they pick any later than that at this point and their chances of getting a better pick feel pretty high right now. Here is a midseason simulation of the first three rounds using Pro Football Focus’ Mock Simulator. While a ton will change between now and late April, this is a good way for us to familiarize ourselves with some prospects to get excited about. Pick 1.05: Jeremiah Smith, Wide Receiver, Ohio State The biggest question going into the Eagles offseason is what happens with the quarterback position. Can Jalen Hurts play football again? Does he want to play football again? Does he want to play football for the Eagles? If the answer to all of these questions is (miraculously) yes, then the Eagles should double down on supplying Hurts with as many weapons as possible. Jeremiah Smith is the best wide receiver prospect since Julio Jones and AJ Green came out of college in 2011. There are no holes in his game and he would immediately be one of the best receivers in the NFL as a rookie. Now imagine him as WR1 with DeVonta Smith on the other side and Makai Lemon in the slot. That is a great way to get Hurts (or any other quarterback) cooking. Pick 2.36: Greg Johnson, IOL, Minnesota The turnover at offensive line this season has been a mess. Injury luck combined with youth at key positions has led to the offensive line being a real problem. Greg Johnson has been a stellar player for the Golden Gophers over the last few years. He has great size and strength, with the ability to thrive at guard or center. He’d be an immediate upgrade for Philly on the inside at all three positions he’d be able to play. Pick 3.97: Boubacar Traore, Edge Defender, Notre Dame One of the many frustrations this season has been the Eagles lack of edge pressure. While Nolan Smith is having a solid year, the rest of the Eagles edge guys have been really mediocre, at best. Boubacar Traore is a bit of a pass rush specialist, at 6’5” and 250 pounds. He has great length and burst. Coming off a dominant game against Miami, Traore is getting some real NFL hype now. Maybe he goes a lot higher than this, but right now this would be a steal for the talented pass rusher.

item.title: Jets' Aaron Glenn shuts down Will McDonald's trade request with six-word response
item.description: Jets' Aaron Glenn shuts down Will McDonald's trade request with six-word response originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Jets lost to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 9 and are now heading towards the 2026 NFL trade deadline with a 2-7 record. It would stand to reason that this team is selling, but with players like Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall not likely to be dealt, the focus will shift to more realistic targets. One of those targets, edge rusher Will McDonald IV, requested a trade Monday morning. However, as NFL Network's Ian Rapoport shared, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn shut down the notion of a trade by sharing a six-word message with reporters that shows his preference with McDonald this season. Aaron Glenn shares firm statement on Will McDonald trade request "Coach Aaron Glenn: 'Will is going to be here.' Essentially, Glenn says they don't want to trade good players," Rapoport shared. This commentary from Glenn makes it clear that the Jets' head coach doesn't want his team to trade away McDonald this season. While the former first-round edge rusher is frustrated in his role on defense, playing less than he has in the last two seasons, the Jets seemingly don't want to trade him. There have been rumors about McDonald being a trade target this season, with likely a few teams eyeing him as an option to upgrade their edge rusher room. MORE : Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade But the Jets have shut down those rumors, and Glenn's latest commentary on a potential trade does that. Glenn is making it clear he wants to keep McDonald, believing good players shouldn't be traded by the Jets. Will general manager Darren Mougey see it the same way? It's an interesting question, especially if the Jets receive quality offers for McDonald this season. The 27-year-old edge rusher is in his fourth NFL season, and with how great rookie David Bailey has looked, it wouldn't be that outrageous for New York to trade McDonald this season for a solid return. This is a situation to monitor, even though Glenn has shut down the trade request made by McDonald. Until the trade deadline has passed, McDonald will remain a potential trade candidate. item.title: Incident-by-incident: Was it a bad weekend for VAR?
item.description: Manchester United's last-gasp equaliser against Aston Villa survived a VAR review for a potential foul [Getty Images] Whisper it quietly, but the statistics say video assistant referee decisions have been pretty good in the Premier League so far this season. The Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel, which looks at every contentious decision and votes whether it is right or wrong, reported just two VAR errors after eight rounds of matches. At the same stage last season, there had been six mistakes. Then came this weekend, during which almost every top-flight game had a controversial decision. BBC Sport looks at most of these situations - there really were too many to do them all - and assesses the likelihood that the KMI Panel will add to the list of errors. Manchester United 4-4 Aston Villa Incident 1: Penalty awarded to Manchester United for a foul by Boubacar Kamara on Matheus Cunha in the 16th minute. Verdict: The spot-kick was awarded because the Villa defender went through Cunha to win the ball. Replays clearly showed the first contact was on the Brazilian's foot. What the KMI Panel might say: This will be a correct decision. Incident 2: Possible foul by Senne Lammens on Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki before Patrick Dorgu's 96th-minute equaliser. Verdict : There are similarities to a goal Arsenal scored at Old Trafford last season, when William Saliba leant into United goalkeeper Altay Bayındır. Lammens was not looking at the ball, which increases the chances of a VAR intervention. What the KMI Panel might say: With the higher bar for an intervention in the Premier League, and minimal contact, it is unlikely to be a VAR error not to disallow the goal. Arsenal 1-0 Hull Incident: Kai Havertz was pulled down inside the area by Nobel Mendy. The VAR, Michael Oliver, sent referee Farai Hallam to the pitchside monitor for a penalty, but it was not given due to an offside offence by the Germany international. Verdict: BBC Sport covered this incident in detail on Saturday . As the foul happened before any potential offside offence, the penalty should have been awarded. What the KMI Panel might say: Even though it feels wrong to reward a player in an offside position with a penalty, the law says otherwise and this is likely to be a mistake. Leeds 1-0 Tottenham Incident: Omar Bogle fouled Mathys Tel, with referee John Brooks giving the free-kick but no sanction for the Leeds player. The VAR, Tony Harrington, opted not to send Brooks to the monitor for a red card. Verdict: BBC Sport covered the merits of this incident on Saturday . It was a difficult call for the VAR, because Bogle caused the foul with his supporting rather than his challenging foot. Still, it was a very painful challenge and some believe it should have been a red card. What the KMI Panel might say: Was it an unfortunate incident, or a tackle which endangered the opponent? item.title: Edo APC chieftain killed by son over alleged prophecy
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Fugar, Etsako Central Local Government Area of Edo State, Julius Bello, has been allegedly killed by his son, Irobudo, following a prophecy that reportedly blamed him for the suspect’s misfortunes. Bello, popularly known as De Lord Ogata, was reportedly attacked with a sledgehammer by his son, who struck him on the head. The incident occurred on Sunday, shortly after the suspect reportedly returned from Lagos at the weekend. Witnesses said the suspect allegedly attacked his father after a prophet told him that Bello was responsible for his poor state in life. The deceased was the APC Ward Three Chairman in Fugar, Etsako Central Local Government Area. The Edo State Police Command confirmed the killing, with its spokesperson, Eno Ikoedem, saying the command had commenced an investigation. The suspect was still at large as of the time of filing this report. The post Edo APC chieftain killed by son over alleged prophecy appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ICPC files amended charge against Adeyemi, adds four civil servants
item.description: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has filed amended charges against Adeniyi Adeyemi, the purported director general of the non-existent Presidential Foreign Intervention Promotion Council (PFIPC). The prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, SAN, told the court that ICPC expanded the previous 22 counts to 36. Tahir said that the four suspects are Aminu Abdullahi, Ogaba Harry, Florence Omameh and Patricia Akhigbe and included in the new charge. The case was originally filed by the Nigerian police. Monday’s proceedings, which originally slated for hearing of Adeyemi’s bail application, was halted because of the charge amendment, requiring all defendants, including Adeyemi, to enter their pleas. However, the plea taking could not proceed because the fourth defendant, Omameh, was absent from court on health grounds. The rest of the defendants were in court. ”Her unavailability in court has constrained the prosecution from proceeding with the arraignment, this being a criminal charge,” Tahir said. He relied on Section 266 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) for his application. Tahir argued that an accused person has to be present in court throughout the trial, “subject to the exception stated therein.” He, therefore, urged the court for a short adjournment to allow the fourth defendant time to recover and enter her plea. Adeyemi’s counsel, Ibrahim Angulu, SAN, did not object to the amended charge or adjournment. However, he reminded the court of Adeyemi’s prolonged detention. Meanwhile, Justice Yusuf Halilu adjourned until Nov. 18 for the arraignment of the suspects. He, however, ordered that Adeyemi should be taken back to Kuje Correctional Facility and the other defendants to return to the ICPC detention facility. (NAN) The post ICPC files amended charge against Adeyemi, adds four civil servants appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Youth Olympics: Nwankwo, Bright Win Historic Gold In Men’s, Women’s 100m
item.description: Nigeria made an impressive start to the athletics competition at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Sunday, winning gold in both the men’s and women’s 100m finals at the Complexe Iba Mar Diop. Rosemary Nwankwo opened the country’s gold-medal account in the women’s 100m, crossing the finish line in 11.16 seconds to claim victory and set a new personal best. Nigeria’s Rosemary Nwankwo, gold medalist (C), Arwa Ali of the United Arab Emirates (L), silver medalist, and Dana Salem of Qatar (R), bronze medalist, pose on the podium after the women’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) She finished ahead of Arwa Ali of the United Arab Emirates, who clocked 11.41 seconds, also a personal best, while Dana Salem of Qatar settled for bronze in 11.48 seconds. The win made Nwankwo the third Nigerian woman to take Youth Olympic 100m gold, following Josephine Omaka at the inaugural Singapore 2010 Games and Rosemary Chukwuma at Buenos Aires 2018. Nigeria’s Rosemary Nwankwo, winner of the women’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, poses next to the board at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) Nigeria’s celebrations continued minutes later as Gift Bright secured another gold medal in the men’s 100m, finishing in a personal-best time of 10.28 seconds. China’s Zhang Hangyu came second in 10.57 seconds, while Poland’s Szymon Dolega claimed bronze in 10.61 seconds. Speaking after her triumph, Nwankwo said she remained focused on her race despite the significance of the occasion. Nigeria’s Gift Bright, react after winning the men’s 100-meter semifinal at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) “There was no pressure on me. I run my race. I focused on me, and I did it,” she said. “I’ve prayed for this moment, and I did it.” For Bright, the victory was particularly significant after a thigh injury had troubled him in the two weeks leading up to the competition. China’s Hangyu Zhang (L), silver medalist; Nigeria’s Gift Bright (C), gold medalist; and Poland’s Szymon Dolega (R), bronze medalist, pose on the podium after the men’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) He admitted that the injury had affected his confidence but said he was relieved to compete without pain in the final. “I want to tell you guys that at the next (Youth) Olympics, expect Nigeria to win it again. We are good sprinters,” he said. We know how to condition ourselves to stay where we are. It’s a very big thing for us.” The post Youth Olympics: Nwankwo, Bright Win Historic Gold In Men’s, Women’s 100m appeared first on

item.title: PIA: Reps demand accountability, measurable benefits for Nigerians
item.description: …Say five years after enactment, reforms must boost production, revenue, investment By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for greater accountability in the management of Nigeria’s petroleum resources, insisting that the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) must deliver increased oil production, higher government revenue, improved energy security, job creation and tangible benefits for Nigerians. The House said five years after the enactment of the legislation, the Federal Government and relevant institutions must demonstrate the impact of the reforms on the country’s oil and gas industry and the wider economy. Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, stated this on Monday at the opening of a three-day retreat on Petroleum Industry Act Implementation: The PIA, Corporate Governance and Legislative Oversight, organised by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) in collaboration with the Office of the Speaker in Abuja. Abbas, who was represented by the House Leader, Julius Ihonvbere, said the success of the PIA should not be measured merely by the establishment of new institutions or the restructuring of the national oil company, but by its ability to deliver value from Nigeria’s petroleum resources. He described the PIA as one of the country’s most consequential economic legislations, designed to establish a transparent, commercially viable, accountable and investment-friendly petroleum industry. “Five years down the line, the central question is how much of that promise we have translated into practice,” he said. The Speaker noted that the transformation of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation into NNPC Ltd, the establishment of regulatory institutions and the introduction of a framework for host community development were intended to address longstanding challenges in the petroleum sector. He, however, stressed that the passage of the legislation must be followed by effective implementation to achieve its objectives. “The passage of a reform law is not the same as the successful implementation of that reform,” Abbas said. He identified crude oil theft, pipeline vandalism, production constraints, infrastructure deficiencies, investment uncertainty and regulatory bottlenecks as major challenges requiring urgent attention. According to him, protecting petroleum infrastructure remains critical to safeguarding national revenue and strengthening the country’s economic and security interests. “We recognise that the protection of national petroleum assets is not merely an industry concern; it is an economic and national security imperative,” he said. Abbas also called for adequate crude oil supplies to domestic refineries without undermining the commercial viability of upstream operations, noting that Nigeria must strengthen its domestic refining capacity and improve energy security. item.title: 2027: Shettima assures South-East of project completion, seeks votes
item.description: …As Nwifuru pledges Ebonyi support for Tinubu By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign train on Monday arrived in Abakaliki, the Ebonyi State capital, to canvass support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 general elections. Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who represented Tinubu at the rally, assured the people of Ebonyi State and the South-East of the completion of ongoing federal projects if the President is re-elected. Shettima also said the Tinubu administration had strengthened security in the South-East, particularly Ebonyi State, creating a safer environment for residents. He urged the electorate to come out en masse to vote for Governor Francis Nwifuru and other APC candidates in the forthcoming elections. In his remarks, Governor Nwifuru pledged the support of Ebonyi voters for Tinubu’s re-election, assuring the President of massive votes from the state. He said the South-East had suffered infrastructure deficits under previous administrations but maintained that the Tinubu government had changed the situation through projects across the region and other parts of the country, many of which are being supervised by the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi. The governor appealed to the Federal Government to connect the southern part of Ebonyi State to the national electricity grid to improve power supply and support industrial development. He also urged Tinubu to approve and ensure the completion of the proposed railway project linking Ebonyi to Aba in Abia State and Port Harcourt in Rivers State. Nwifuru highlighted some achievements of his administration in the last three and a half years, particularly in the health and education sectors. He said his government had provided medical equipment and revitalised primary and secondary healthcare facilities across the state’s 13 local government areas. The governor also disclosed that work had commenced on the Abakaliki cement factory project, expressing optimism that its completion would create employment opportunities for young people. On education, he said his administration had recruited teachers for primary and secondary schools, adding that 314 beneficiaries of state scholarships had graduated with master’s degrees from overseas universities and commenced doctoral programmes in the United Kingdom. Also speaking, Umahi said Ebonyi State remained an APC stronghold and urged residents to support Tinubu’s second-term ambition to enable the administration to complete ongoing infrastructure projects. The minister listed several federal projects in the state, including the Afikpo-Cross River Ndibe Bridge, the Abakaliki-Afikpo road dualisation and the proposed superhighway linking Ebonyi, Enugu, Kogi, Benue, Nasarawa and Abuja. item.title: Obi Alleges NFF Blocked Him From Greeting Victorious Flamingos
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi has alleged that officials of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) prevented him from greeting members of the national Under-17 women’s football team, the Flamingos, following their historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Obi said he was allegedly informed that the officials had warned against allowing him to approach the players, allegedly threatening that they would lose their jobs if he did. The former Anambra State governor disclosed this in a statement posted on his official X handle on Monday, after the Flamingos returned to Nigeria following their 2-1 victory over Japan in Saturday’s final in Morocco. Obi said he arrived at the airport at about 7 a.m. on Monday to board a flight to Enugu when he sighted the victorious team preparing to leave the airport. Flamingos arriving in Nigeria. He said he subsequently asked his protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether he could greet and welcome the players. “With genuine joy and enthusiasm, I asked my Protocol Officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether I could greet and welcome the team. I was informed that officials of the Nigerian Football Federation (NFF) had refused and had requested that I not approach them because, if I did, they would all lose their jobs,” he wrote. Obi described the incident as another example of what he called the growing culture of “toxic politics” in Nigeria, alleging that he had experienced similar treatment during a previous visit to a football event. He recounted that on March 25, 2025, he travelled to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, for a World Cup qualifying match, where he said the governor received him at the VIP stand. According to him, after the match, other government officials were allowed to greet the players, but he was again prevented from doing so. “Following the match, other government officials went to greet the players, but I was again prevented from doing so. I was told by the officials that they would lose their jobs if I proceeded,” he said. The former governor expressed concern over what he described as the increasing politicisation of public engagements, arguing that political differences should not prevent Nigerians from celebrating national achievements. “It is deeply troubling to witness the extent of toxic politics into which our nation has descended since 2025. Each year appears to bring further deterioration. This reflects how deeply Nigeria has been affected. “The new Nigeria we aspire to build must have no room for hostility, intimidation, or discrimination, regardless of political affiliation. It must be a Nigeria in which unity, mutual respect, and our shared humanity take,” he said. item.title: Who Gives A Crap? Hackers, apparently, after toilet paper maker's customer data exposed
item.description: Toilet paper purveyor Who Gives A Crap has found itself in a bit of a mess after an intruder accessed customer information through a third-party software provider, leaving the company scrambling to clean up a breach affecting shoppers in the UK, US, and Australia. In an email sent to affected customers over the weekend, seen by The Register , the loo roll seller warns that personal information was accessed without authorization after a security incident at an unnamed US-based marketing software provider. The email explains that the intruder gained access to the supplier's systems on October 30. The provider spotted the intrusion the following day and says it secured its systems by November 1, although Who Gives A Crap wasn't told until November 6. It's unclear why the supplier sat on the bad news for another five days before passing it on. The exposed information includes customers' names, email addresses, phone numbers, mailing addresses, and total spending with the company. In other words, someone may now know not only where you live, but just how much of your hard-earned cash you've flushed down the crapper. Payment information, order details, and passwords were not involved, and customers' accounts were not directly accessed. That's something of a relief, although whether the intruder actually made off with the data remains a pressing question. "We don't yet know whether the information was copied or downloaded," the company told customers, adding that it had found no evidence of misuse. In a separate public statement , Who Gives A Crap co-founder and CEO Simon Griffiths confirmed that the incident affected customers across the company's Australian, UK, and US stores. Canadian customers, meanwhile, appear to have escaped this particular toilet emergency, with the supplier reporting that no personal information belonging to shoppers in the country was accessed. Who Gives A Crap says it has since disconnected the provider from its systems, changed access credentials, and begun warning affected customers to watch out for suspicious emails, texts, calls, and other unsolicited communications. "The main concern is scam or phishing messages that use your real details to look convincing," the company warned in its customer email. While Who Gives A Crap has been busy cleaning up, the supplier at the center of this particular stink remains a mystery. The company hasn't identified the software provider or disclosed how many customers were affected, including those in the UK, and didn’t respond to our questions. Griffiths said the company is "engaging with the relevant regulatory authorities, as required." In the UK, the ICO told The Register : "We can confirm Who Gives A Crap Limited has reported an incident and we are assessing the information provided." Who Gives A Crap has plenty of toilet paper to hand, although cleaning up this particular situation might require more than a few rolls. ®

item.title: SpaceX will launch epic double-catch Starship Flight 15 test mission on Nov. 13
item.description: null SpaceX will make spaceflight history this week, if all goes according to plan. The company announced over the weekend that it's targeting Friday (Nov. 13) for the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket, which will attempt something that's never been done before. "The upcoming flight is planned to be the first to return both Starship and Super Heavy to the launch site for catch," SpaceX wrote in a description of Flight 15 . "If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket." SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 14th test flight on Sept. 28, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) Super Heavy is Starship's giant booster, and Starship (or Ship for short) is its upper-stage spacecraft. As SpaceX's description noted, both elements are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable. "Catch" refers to SpaceX's recovery mechanism for both stages: Each will return to the launch mount at SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas and be plucked out of the sky by the tower's "chopstick" arms. SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on three Starship flights to date, but it has never tried the maneuver with Ship. It's a taller order; Ship flies higher and farther than Super Heavy, so its return to Earth is more complex and energetic. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk already told us that Flight 15 would likely feature a double-catch attempt . But the newly released mission description gives us a launch date, as well as details about the flight. Starship Die Cast Rocket Model Was $47.99 Now $39.99 on Amazon . item.title: Ogun govt clarifies video of corps members sleeping in hall
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Ogun State Government has described a viral video showing prospective corps members sleeping in a hall at the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) Orientation Camp in Sagamu, following concerns over accommodation conditions at the facility. The state government said the situation occurred during the registration exercise, which extended into the night, adding that the allocation of hostels and screening of prospective corps members were the exclusive responsibilities of NYSC officials. Special Adviser on Media and Strategy to Governor Dapo Abiodun, Kayode Akinmade, in a Facebook post on Monday, explained that prospective corps members were required to undergo credential verification and screening before being assigned accommodation. He said those whose registration extended into the night were temporarily accommodated in the multipurpose hall, where mattresses were provided for them to rest while the exercise continued. He stated: “The video captured a temporary arrangement during the registration exercise, which continued into the night. “The prospective corps members must first undergo credential verification and screening by NYSC officials before being allocated hostels. Those whose registration extended into the night were temporarily accommodated in the multipurpose hall, with mattresses provided for them to rest while the exercise continued.” Akinmade noted that Ogun State received more than 4,300 prospective corps members in the current batch, compared with slightly over 2,000 in previous batches, putting additional pressure on available camp facilities. He stressed that although NYSC handles registration, screening and hostel allocation, the state government supports the scheme through interventions aimed at improving the welfare of corps members. According to him, the state government provided 500 mattresses for the current exercise, while the Akarigbo of Remo donated 100 mattresses, followed by an additional 200. Akinmade also recalled that Governor Abiodun recently approved a ₦50,000 welfare grant for each of the 3,050 corps members in the 2026 Batch C, Stream I, to support their transportation. He added that Ogun State had been adjudged the best in the country in NYSC administration, describing the recognition as a reflection of the government’s sustained commitment to the scheme. The government urged the public to distinguish between the operational responsibilities of NYSC and the supportive role of the state, assuring that the Abiodun administration would continue to provide an enabling environment for corps members serving in Ogun. item.title: Strive (ASST) Adds 29 Bitcoin for $2.2 Million as Weekly Buys Slow After Crossing 43,000
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Adds 29 Bitcoin for $2.2 Million as Weekly Buys Slow After Crossing 43,000 Strive bought another 29 bitcoin last week for about $2.2 million at an average of $75,721 per coin between Oct. 31 and Nov. 6, a Monday 8-K filing shows , lifting total holdings to 43,153 BTC from 43,124 as of Oct. 30 and capping a month that had already pushed the Dallas treasury past 40,000 coins. Chairman and CEO Matthew Cole posted the same figures on X: “Strive acquired 29 $BTC for $2.2M at an average cost of $75,721 per bitcoin, bringing total holdings to ₿43,153.” Strive’s corporate account republished the note minutes later. The average price is inclusive of fees and expenses, the filing says. The buy is a sharp downshift from the pace Strive set through October. The prior week alone, from Oct. 24 through Oct. 30, Strive added 124 bitcoin at about $80,526 a coin. Between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30 the company acquired 15,124 bitcoin in total, and Friday’s third-quarter results put year-to-date bitcoin yield — Strive’s measure of the percentage change in bitcoin per share — at 63.2% through Sept. 30, with an 18.5% print for the third quarter alone. Holdings stood at 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 before the October sprint. That climb followed multi-thousand-coin buys earlier this fall, including a 6,182-coin purchase funded with preferred proceeds, and kept Strive among the largest public corporate stacks after Strategy. Cash, SATS and a thinner weekly add Cash and cash equivalents fell to $487.6 million as of Nov. 6 from $490.4 million a week earlier, a $2.8 million drop that roughly covers the roughly $2.2 million bitcoin spend plus fees. Strive did not break out a separate funding line for this week’s coins in the 8-K. The preferred stack kept moving. Shares of Strive’s 15% Series A perpetual preferred ( SATS ) rose by 33,141 to 7,036,559, a tally that includes shares sold through 4:00 p.m. Eastern that settle the next business day. SATA preferred stock was unchanged at 14,030,176. Effective common shares outstanding held flat at 127,331,109 after a Class A increase of 15,382 was offset by a matching Class B decline. Strive still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred, marked at a fair value of $50.4 million as of Nov. 6, up slightly from $50.1 million a week earlier. The company closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds and later lined up a $1 billion SATS at-the-market program, tools that have funded the larger buys that built the stack and that still leave room to keep adding if the ATM finds buyers. At bitcoin near $74,650, the 43,153-coin treasury is worth roughly $3.22 billion on paper. That marks the stack about 1.4% under this week’s $75,721 average purchase price, though Strive has not disclosed a companywide cost basis in Monday’s filing the way Strategy does each week. item.title: Coinbase Wins Full Federal Trust Charter From OCC
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Wins Full Federal Trust Charter From OCC Coinbase has won a full national trust bank charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, upgrading the conditional approval it received in April and putting its institutional custody business under direct federal supervision, the exchange said Monday. The OCC approved the application for Coinbase National Trust Company last Friday, the company said in a blog post. OCC licensing records, as reported, show the chartering process was completed Nov. 6. Coinbase applied in October 2025 and received preliminary approval on April 2. In the intervening months it had to finish its organizational and operational preparations before the OCC would let the trust bank open. “This charter allows us to bring clear and consistent federal uniformity to our industry-leading custody capabilities,” Coinbase wrote, adding that it strengthens the regulatory framework under which it serves customers. The company said it has served as a custodian for more than 14 years. What the charter allows A national trust bank can hold assets for clients as a fiduciary, and Coinbase’s focus is custody for institutional customers. It is not a commercial bank. It cannot take ordinary retail deposits or make loans, and the charter does not authorize it to issue stablecoins. Staking, prime trading and financing will keep running through Coinbase affiliates, not the trust itself. Under the OCC’s April decision, the trust bank acts as an intermediary for those services and does not perform them directly. The decision also sets conditions. The trust bank must hold at least $60 million in Tier 1 capital and enough liquid assets to cover 180 days of operating expenses during its first three years. The license does not automatically connect Coinbase to Federal Reserve payment systems either. That requires a separate application under the Fed’s account access guidelines. Coinbase already runs custody through Coinbase Custody Trust Company, a limited-purpose trust regulated by the New York State Department of Financial Services. The company plans to move that business to the national entity over three years. A crowded charter queue Coinbase is the latest crypto firm to complete a federal trust charter. Ripple received final approval on Oct. 26, and Circle won final OCC approval in July, a decision that put USDC reserves on a path toward federal supervision. The OCC has been courting the sector. In August, Comptroller Jonathan V. Gould said “America and the OCC are once again open for business,” as the regulator touted its charter push. Ripple, Circle, Crypto.com and Paxos had all received conditional approval by then. Block applied for its own banking charter in September. The approval did not come without resistance.
