item.title: Meet only 2 countries to have won both men’s, women’s U-17 World Cups
item.description: Nigeria and France have emerged as the only two countries to have won both the men’s and women’s FIFA Under-17 World Cups following the Flamingos’ historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Nigeria achieved the milestone after its U-17 women’s team defeated Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final in Rabat, becoming the first African nation to win the women’s competition. The victory also ended Nigeria’s 18-year wait for a FIFA U-17 title, having last won the men’s competition in 2015. According to FIFA’s records, France were previously the only country to have won both versions of the tournament, having secured the men’s title in 2001 and the women’s trophy in 2012. Nigeria’s five men’s U-17 World Cup titles Nigeria’s success in the men’s competition dates back to 1985, when the Golden Eaglets defeated West Germany 2-0 in Beijing to win the inaugural edition of the tournament, then known as the FIFA U-16 World Championship. The team went on to win the competition four more times, in 1993, 2007, 2013 and 2015. Its five titles make Nigeria the most successful country in the history of the men’s U-17 World Cup. The 2013 triumph came after a 3-0 victory over Mexico in the final, while the 2015 team defeated Mali 2-0 in Chile to become the first country to win consecutive editions of the tournament. How France achieved the double France became the first country to win both versions of the competition. The French men’s team won the 2001 FIFA U-17 World Championship in Trinidad and Tobago after defeating Nigeria 3-0 in the final. Eleven years later, France’s women’s team lifted the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Azerbaijan in 2012. They defeated North Korea 7-6 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the final to claim their maiden title. France therefore held the distinction of being the only country to have won both competitions until Nigeria’s latest achievement. Flamingos end Nigeria’s long wait Nigeria’s historic achievement was secured through a 2-1 victory over Japan in the 2026 final. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring in the 39th minute before Oluebube Umejiaku doubled Nigeria’s advantage two minutes into the second half. Japan reduced the deficit through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute, but the Flamingos held on to secure the trophy. The victory completed a remarkable campaign for the Nigerian side, which recovered from a 2-1 opening defeat to Poland to win its next six matches. The team also defeated Brazil 3-1 in the semi-finals to book its place in the final against Japan. The triumph was significant beyond Nigeria, as it marked the first time an African country had won the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. It also made the Flamingos the first Nigerian women’s national team to win a FIFA World Cup title. With the latest achievement, Nigeria joins France in the exclusive group of countries to have won both the men’s and women’s FIFA U-17 World Cups. item.title: History in Morocco! How Nigeria’s Flamingos Won the World Cup
item.description: The Flamingos celebrate on stage with green and white confetti as they lift the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup trophy. History was made in Rabat as the Flamingos of Nigeria conquered global football at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Under head coach Akeem Busari , the team executed an extraordinary seven-match campaign at the finals, overcoming an early setback to claim six consecutive victories and become the first African nation to lift any FIFA women’s international trophy. Midfielder Oluebube Umejiaku earned individual recognition by winning the FIFA Golden Ball as the Player of the Tournament alongside Player of the Match honors in the final. The squad also displayed exceptional attacking breadth, scoring goals through eight different players across seven matches at the finals while registering over 100 goal attempts. Oluebube Umejiaku poses with the FIFA Golden Ball and Player of the Match awards following Nigeria’s World Cup triumph. Here is the match-by-match breakdown of how Nigeria navigated the African qualifiers, powered through the World Cup group stage, defeated multi-time global champions in the knockouts, and clinched the ultimate trophy in Morocco. Nigeria’s Flamingos celebrate becoming the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Japan 2-1 in Rabat. Phase 1: The African Qualifying Journey Nigeria entered the African U-17 World Cup qualifying campaign in the second round, establishing dominance in home-and-away aggregate ties across West Africa. The Flamingos opened their qualification run with an emphatic 5–0 away victory in Guinea, led by team captain Harmony Chidi ’s first-half hat-trick alongside goals from Oluwakemi Adegbuyi and Mary Dunstan . They followed up with a 7–0 victory in the home leg in Ogun State to complete a 12–0 aggregate shutout. The Flamingos celebrate on the pitch following their matchday four fixture at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. In the final qualifying round, Nigeria established a three-goal lead in Monrovia by defeating Liberia 4–1, thanks to a brace from Harmony Chidi and goals from Shakirat Moshood and Peace Effiong . Chidi then sealed a 2–0 second-leg win back home to finish the qualifiers with 12 goals and secure Nigeria’s ticket to Morocco. Phase 2: Group B at the World Cup (Morocco) Placed in Group B alongside Poland, Puerto Rico, and defending world champions DPR Korea, Nigeria had to battle through one of the tournament’s most competitive pools. The campaign started with a tight 2–1 loss to Poland in Rabat, putting pressure on the team to perform in their remaining fixtures. The Flamingos bounced back immediately with a 2–0 shutout victory over Puerto Rico to claim their first three points. Nigeria’s Flamingos celebrate their historic 3-1 Group B victory over defending champions DPR Korea in Morocco. In their final group match, Nigeria produced one of the tournament’s biggest tactical upsets by defeating two-time defending champions DPR Korea

item.title: Presidency tackles Obi over alleged prevention from greeting Flamingos
item.description: The Presidency has accused opposition politicians of attempting to politicise Nigeria’s national sports teams, following a claim by former Anambra State governor, Peter Obi, that he was prevented from greeting members of the victorious Flamingos at an airport. The Special Assistant to the President on Social Media, Dada Olusegun, made the position known in a post on X on Monday, describing attempts to politicise national sports teams and institutions as distasteful. Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, had alleged that officials of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) stopped him from approaching the Under-17 women’s national team after their return from the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Reacting to the allegation, Olusegun said national athletes, including the Flamingos, represented the entire country rather than any political party or individual. He explained that protocols governing national teams were designed to protect young athletes from political exploitation, commercial distractions and unnecessary media attention while on official duties. “The constant attempt by the opposition to politicize our national sports teams and institutions is highly distasteful,” he wrote. “Our national athletes, including the Under-17 girls’ team, represent the entire Federal Republic of Nigeria, not any specific political party or individual ambition. Protocol guidelines around national teams are designed strictly to protect young athletes from political exploitation, commercial distractions, and unnecessary media circuses while on official duty.” Addressing Obi directly, the presidential aide urged him to reconsider what he described as his tendency to manipulate situations and rely on unverified accounts to create a narrative of victimisation. “Mr Peter Obi, I hope you will reflect on your manipulative way of life and stop weaponising unverified hearsay to build a victim narrative. Let our athletes focus on winning for Nigeria, free from political theatre,” he wrote. Obi had earlier said he arrived at the airport around 7am on Monday while preparing to travel to Enugu when he sighted the Flamingos, who had just returned from Morocco. He said he asked his protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether he could welcome the players but was informed that NFF officials had objected to his approach. According to Obi, the officials reportedly warned that they would lose their jobs if they allowed him to greet the team. The former governor also recalled an earlier incident on March 25, 2025, when he travelled to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, for a World Cup qualifying match and was allegedly prevented from greeting members of Nigeria’s national team after the game. Expressing concern over what he described as a growing culture of toxic politics, Obi said the country should prioritise unity and mutual respect regardless of political differences. The Flamingos returned to Abuja on Monday following their 2-1 victory over Japan

item.title: Why I rejected Tinubu’s ministerial offer — Tunde Bakare
item.description: The Leader of Citadel Global Community Church, Pastor Tunde Bakare, has explained why he declined an offer by President Bola Tinubu to serve as a minister in his administration, saying he considered himself too old for the responsibilities of the office. Bakare said he preferred to support the government from behind the scenes by offering advice and proposing solutions to national challenges. The cleric disclosed this on Sunday while speaking at an event organised by Envoy Nation in Leicester, United Kingdom. He said he had told Tinubu that although he was not interested in joining his cabinet, he remained willing to contribute to national development through constructive advice whenever necessary. Bakare clarified that his decision to stay outside the government should not be interpreted as opposition to the Tinubu administration, insisting that he had never belonged to the opposition. He described himself as a platform for constructive suggestions, saying he would speak out whenever he identified shortcomings in government policies or actions and offer possible solutions. The former presidential candidate also reaffirmed his membership of the All Progressives Congress (APC), dismissing suggestions that he could easily switch political allegiance. He said, “I told Tinubu I’m too old to be a minister, but I will help in the background in any way I think will help my country. I have never been part of the opposition. I am a propositional platform, if I see something wrong, I will suggest a solution. “I can’t change sides quickly by joining one party today and another tomorrow. I am a full member of APC, and I will vote when the time comes.” Bakare’s remarks underscore his preference for contributing to governance through private counsel and constructive criticism rather than holding a formal position in the Tinubu administration. item.title: The AI bubble can wait, but your exit plan can't
item.description: The AI bubble isn't about to burst, Forrester reckons, although businesses should prepare for a correction that could upend their suppliers, contracts, and prices. Spending on infrastructure has raced ahead of measurable returns, the analyst says, yet the financial strength of the companies funding the build-out is what keep Forrester from predicting an imminent crash. "Fears that an AI bubble is about to burst are premature," said Forrester emerging technology veep Brian Hopkins. "About nine-tenths of the money building today's AI computing infrastructure comes from large, healthy technology companies paying out of their own cash flow. The risk is concentrated in a few places: a small number of builders under real financial strain, and circular financing deals with the AI labs." Conveniently, Forrester has developed an AI Bubble Model to help technology leaders monitor the risks and prepare. Its latest report, " An AI Bubble Burst Is Not Imminent ," notes what many in the IT industry, including The Register , have been saying for a while: that the hyperscale operators are committing a record share of revenue into capital expenditure to bring online more infrastructure to support AI development and use. At the same time, the boost in productivity doesn't justify this supplier capacity build-out. Forrester calculates that the infrastructure investments break even only if AI raises US GDP by 5 percent by 2035. Published estimates suggest productivity improvements could provide about two percentage points of that uplift, leaving roughly $1.3 trillion to come from other sources of value. A recent report from management consultants Bain & Company came to similar conclusions, estimating the AI industry needs to generate $6 trillion in annual revenue by 2031 to keep funding all the infrastructure it needs, and this will require new uses beyond simply enhancing employee productivity. Forrester also claims that the forces making AI abundant also make parts of the market unstable, and says that enterprise users should take heed of how prices collapsed as major providers like Anthropic slashed token costs in response to competition from open source models. If demand disappoints as new capacity comes online, suppliers could cut investment, merge, change prices, or discontinue products. Customers could find themselves rebuilding AI plans around suppliers and services that no longer exist. Forrester advises businesses to track whether their AI projects deliver measurable value and limit their exposure to vulnerable suppliers – with its help, of course. Companies can judge how things are going by looking at the gap between suppliers' contracted business and revenue actually recognized, along with how they fund their build-outs. If a vendor leans more on outside investment and customer prepayments, as Oracle and CoreWeave have, this is a red flag to cut back dependencies on them, Forrester says. item.title: UK lists categories of migrants who can secure permanent residence after 5 years
item.description: The UK government has outlined categories of foreign nationals who will remain eligible to obtain permanent residence after five years, despite plans to extend the standard settlement period for most migrants to 10 years. Under its revised Earned Settlement policy, announced by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood on November 2, 2026, the government intends to replace the existing five-year standard route to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) with a system that rewards migrants based on their earnings, professional contributions and immigration history. However, certain categories of migrants will retain access to the five-year settlement pathway. According to the Home Office, the exemptions are intended to recognise the contributions of higher-earning migrants, essential public service workers and people who have served the UK through specific immigration routes. Migrants who can qualify for permanent residence after five years The following groups have been identified under the revised settlement framework: 1. High-earning foreign workers Migrants earning more than £50,271 annually will be eligible to apply for permanent residence after five years, provided they meet the income requirement for at least three of the five years preceding their application. This category covers foreign professionals whose earnings meet the government’s specified threshold. 2. Doctors, nurses and teachers Foreign nationals working in qualifying healthcare and education occupations will retain the five-year settlement pathway. The government specifically identified doctors, nurses and teachers as examples of professionals whose contributions to essential public services justify a shorter route to permanent residence. 3. Eligible care workers Care workers who entered or switched into the social care route during the period between 2022 and 2025 will retain the opportunity to secure permanent residence after five years. However, they must have complied with their visa conditions and earned at least £25,000 annually while working in the social care sector. The government said the exemption recognises the contribution of care workers during the period when Britain’s social care sector faced significant staffing shortages following the COVID-19 pandemic. 4. Eligible family members of British citizens Certain partners, parents and children of British citizens will also retain access to the five-year settlement pathway. The exemption covers eligible family visa applicants, although the precise eligibility conditions will depend on the applicable immigration rules. 5. Refugees arriving through approved safe and legal routes Foreign nationals granted refugee status after arriving in the UK through government-approved safe and legal routes will be eligible to apply for permanent residence after five years. item.title: Meteorite that landed in Cape Cod was a 'lone wolf' from the outer solar system, scientists find
item.description: Thanks to a combination of radar, infrasound, dash-cam and security camera footage, astronomers have tracked the bright daytime meteor that fell over Cape Cod Bay in May 2026 back to its origin as a small asteroid perturbed by Jupiter and sent on a comet-like orbit towards Earth. Meteor fireballs visible in the daytime are referred to as 'bolides'. At 1:06 p.m. local time (18:06 UTC) on May 30, 2026 one such bolide was widely witnessed falling out of the sky over coastal Massachusetts, with members of the public also reporting an associated sonic boom that rumbled across the north-eastern coast of the United States. Now, a team of scientists from Europe and the United States, led by space physicist Juha Vierinen of the Arctic University of Norway in Tromsø, have patched together measurements from a meteor-observing radar network, regular weather radar, infrasound stations and camera footage to fully characterize the fall of this meteoroid and trace its orbit around the sun . Key to these observations were measurements by the Spread Spectrum Interferometric Meteor Observing Network (SIMONe) based at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology's (MIT's) Haystack Observatory. SIMONe is a project jointly developed by MIT, the Arctic University of Norway and the Leibniz Institute of Atmospheric Physics in Kühlungsborn, Germany. "We were fortunate that the event occurred within the coverage of SIMONe," Vierinen told Space.com. This is echoed by Ryan Volz, a radio scientist at Haystack Observatory who is a member of the team who studied the May 30 bolide. "We got pretty lucky to observe this one," Volz told Space.com. "A bolide like this would have to enter the atmosphere within about 62 miles (100 kilometers) of a SIMONe-like meteor radar system for the head echoes we saw to be detectable, and there are only a handful of places in the world that currently meet that criteria." A head echo is what radar sees when a meteoroid – what we call the lump of rock that becomes a meteor while it is still in space – enters Earth's atmosphere , generating a cloud of plasma around it as it superheats the atmosphere and its outer surface. "The head echoes give the best constraints on the meteoroid's trajectory," said Volz. The existence of the head echo is usually very brief, taking place at 56 miles (90 kilometers () altitude down to about 44 miles (71 kilometers) when the plasma around the meteoroid is dense enough to return a radar echo. The head echo transitions into a 'trail echo', which is produced by a streak of turbulent plasma that is left in the wake of the meteoroid after it has passed through a given part of the atmosphere. In the case of the 30 May bolide, the trail echo was detected down to an unusually low altitude of 20 miles (32 kilometers), at which point the falling rock fragmented with an explosive force equivalent to 500 tons of TNT, whereas the total impact energy of the bolide was in the region on 1.1 kilotons of TNT. item.title: Bitcoin Price Drops Below $74,000 as Nvidia Probe and Regulation Fears Spark $1 Billion in Liquidations
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Drops Below $74,000 as Nvidia Probe and Regulation Fears Spark $1 Billion in Liquidations Bitcoin price traded near $74,700 on Monday morning after sliding to $73,477 overnight, its lowest since August, then bouncing back, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. Bitcoin price fell more than 2% to $73,477 in overnight trading, its lowest since August. Buyers stepped in soon after and pushed the price back above $75,000, but the bounce stalled and the bitcoin price settled near $74,700 into the New York open. Nvidia probe and Iran stall hit weekend trading Crypto was the only major market open when two headlines landed. Nvidia faced an internal investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iranian demands were outrageous as talks stalled. Nvidia is the bellwether of the AI trade that has carried risk assets all year, so traders treated the news as a threat to the whole complex. More than $1 billion of leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours and about $913 million of that came from longs, which turned a dip into a sharp flush. The stock market delivered a calmer opening. U.S. index futures attempted a recovery as investors hunted for bargains, with Dow futures up 0.73%, S&P 500 futures up 0.40% and Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.21% at 5:10 a.m. ET. Nvidia shares were down 4.5% in premarket trading, Reuters said, and some chipmakers slipped after the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index posted its biggest weekly loss since March 2025. That split mirrors Friday, when the bitcoin price reaction to a hot jobs report showed crypto sitting out an equity bounce. It also echoes the tech rout that wiped out leveraged longs last Thursday. Regulation fears and ETF outflows weigh on the bitcoin price The other driver is Washington. Reuters tied the weekend drop to fears that a Democratic-controlled Congress will toughen oversight of the asset class, after last week’s midterms and the $6 billion Binance heist. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, one of the loudest crypto critics in the Senate, is tipped to lead the Senate Banking Committee. TD Cowen has warned that the sweep makes a crypto-backed CLARITY Act nearly impossible , and House Democrats are already eyeing their own market structure bill with a bigger role for the SEC. Institutional money is voting too. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs shed $1.28 billion last week, their second straight week of outflows and the worst since late June. Those redemptions explain why the bitcoin price never joined the equity rebound. What the market watches next October consumer price data on Tuesday is the next test. Economists expect headline inflation to rise 0.3% on the month, cooling from 0.6% in September, and futures imply roughly an 80% chance of a Fed hike at the Dec. 8 and 9 meeting after the strong October jobs report. Options traders are bracing for more movement. One-week implied volatility for bitcoin has jumped

item.title: Offa bank robbery: Kwara govt drops 18 charges against Saraki, Ahmed
item.description: … add two new charges By Demola Akinyemi Ilorin In a dramatic twist, the Kwara State Government has filed an amendment to its initial 20-count charge against its two former governors, Dr Abubakar Bukola Saraki and Alhaji Abdulfatai Ahmed, over the 2018 Offa bank robbery case by dropping 18 of the original charges while retaining only two and adding two new charges. In the amended charge sheet with Charge Number KWS/114C/2026 signed by the State Attorney General, Senior Ibrahim Sulyman (SAN), sighted by journalists in Ilorin, the government by implication has now reduced the total number of charges to four. In the new charge sheet, Counts 1 and 2 accused Saraki, Ahmed, Yusuf Abdulwahab and Alabi Olalekan of “conspiring to belong to a gang of thieves” and “belonging to a gang of thieves”. Also, counts 3 and 4, accused the quartet of concealment and disappearance of a “vehicle used for illegal purpose”. A motion on notice for the amended charges dated November 6th, 2026, has been filed by the prosecution and supported by a 6-paragraph affidavit deposed to by Sulyman Mohammed-Jamiu, a litigation clerk in the office of the Kwara State AG. It will be recalled that at the last sitting of the State High Court on the case on November 5th, 2026, the judge, Justice Osuolale Ajayi, reserved his ruling on the issue of whether he could continue with the arraignment while the defendant has a pending application for a stay of proceedings on the matter at the Court of Appeal. The Court of Appeal on November 3rd, 2026, advised the lawyer, Abdulfatah Ahmed, J. A. Mumini, SAN, to formally make his application for the court to issue an order that the parties at the trial court should maintain status quo ante bellum instead of the oral submission that he made to the court. The appellate court then adjourned the case to November 12, 2026. The case at the trial court which commenced in April 2026 has not proceeded to trial as the court is still mired in several preliminary issues which have been taken to the appellate court. Contacted, a member of Saraki and Ahmed’s legal team described the struggle by the prosecution to press charges against the two former governors as “a mockery of the judicial process and an exercise in futility”. Vanguard reliably gathered that failure to make any headway by the Kwara state government may not be unconnected to the two pieces of legal advice issued in 2018 by the Office of the Federal Director of Public Prosecutions in the Office of the Attorney General of the Federation, who, after reviewing the police investigation file on the Offa robbery case in 2018, concluded that there is no evidence remotely or directly linking Saraki or Ahmed to the Offa robbery incident. item.title: Strategy (MSTR) Adds 1,036 Bitcoin for $81.9 Million as Holdings Slip Below Cost
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategy (MSTR) Adds 1,036 Bitcoin for $81.9 Million as Holdings Slip Below Cost Strategy bought another 1,036 bitcoin last week. The Saylor-led firm spent $81.9 million at an average of $79,012 per coin between November 2 and November 8, a Monday 8-K filing shows, lifting total holdings to 850,364 BTC bought for $64.16 billion at an average of $75,456. The coins were funded with net proceeds from MSTR common stock sales. Strategy sold about 2.05 million shares for $283.8 million, put $81.9 million into bitcoin, spent $188.3 million buying back its STRC preferred and parked $13.6 million in USD cash. No preferred stock was sold under the ATM during the week. That buyback retired about 1.89 million STRC shares. Strategy still has $560.3 million left under its preferred repurchase program and $1.0 billion under its MSTR buyback authorization, with about $18.3 billion of MSTR still available under the ATM. Executive Chairman Michael Saylor posted the update on X: “Strategy has acquired 1,036 $BTC and repurchased $188M of $STRC. As of 11/8/26, we hold 850,364 BTC and $4.9B of USD Assets.” On Sunday he shared his usual “dots” tracker chart with the line “Connecting the dots,” a tease that has often preceded Monday buy filings. The chart landed after a weekend slide that pushed bitcoin toward $74,000, its weakest level since August. A thin cushion under Strategy’s treasury The filing lands as the spot bitcoin price sits below Strategy’s average cost. At the time of writing it trades near $74,800, about 0.9% under the $75,456 basis, leaving the stack roughly $550 million underwater on paper. The prior week’s average cost was $75,451, so the new purchase nudged the basis up by only $5 even though those 1,036 coins were bought at nearly $79,000. Strategy’s ledger shows that was not the first time the firm has run a thin cushion this year. Between June 30 and August 10 it sold bitcoin in four consecutive filings — 1,363, then 2,225, then 1,638, then 1,690 coins — to fund preferred dividends and STRC buybacks before flipping back to accumulation. Those sales cut the stack to 840,447 BTC at their low. Strategy has since rebuilt past that mark and now holds more than 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap. The pace of buying has slowed since the summer sales. Strategy added 811 bitcoin the week before this one and skipped buys entirely the week of October 19 through 25 while spending about $205 million on STRC. What the preferred buybacks leave open STRC is designed to trade near its $100 par. Strategy has spent more than $2 billion retiring the preferred this year as the shares oscillated around that level, and shareholders recently approved daily dividends on STRC, STRF, STRK and STRD. Daily accrual for STRC began November 1. This week’s mix put more ATM cash into preferred buybacks than into bitcoin. item.title: UK issues guide for Nigerians, other nationals on accessing eVisa
item.description: The United Kingdom has released guidelines explaining how visa holders, including Nigerians, can access their electronic immigration status. UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) published the instructions in an infographic shared on its official X account on Monday, outlining the process of setting up an account, confirming one’s identity and connecting it to an eVisa. An eVisa is an online record containing a person’s identity and immigration status. It shows the category of permission granted to an individual, including whether they have indefinite leave to remain in the UK, as well as the conditions attached to their immigration status. The UK government said electronic visas have replaced physical immigration documents, adding that individuals granted a UK visa or other permission to remain in the country would be issued an eVisa. How to apply for and access a UK eVisa 1. Submit a visa application Applicants must first complete the UK visa application process through the government’s official website, GOV.UK . Depending on the category of application, they may also need to provide biometric details and verify their identity at a designated Visa Application Centre. 2. Receive an application decision After submitting their applications, applicants will be notified by email once UK Visas and Immigration reaches a decision. The agency advises applicants to monitor their spam and junk folders to ensure they do not miss important notifications. 3. Set up a UKVI account Those whose applications are approved should proceed to create an account through the official eVisa portal at gov.uk/evisa. Applicants are required to follow the online instructions until the system confirms that their accounts have been successfully created. 4. Confirm identity and connect the eVisa After creating an account, users must log in and verify their identities using the UK Immigration: ID Check application. They are also required to link their UKVI accounts to their electronic immigration records to make the eVisas accessible online. 5. Access the electronic visa Once the eVisa is available, users will receive an email notification directing them to view their immigration status online. UKVI advises holders to review their digital records and ensure that all personal and immigration details are accurate before travelling. The UK government says creating a UKVI account and viewing an eVisa are free of charge. The post UK issues guide for Nigerians, other nationals on accessing eVisa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Outlook.com bounces legit emails as Microsoft's authentication crackdown goes sideways
item.description: A validation error has stopped Outlook.com from accepting legitimate emails. The problem appears widespread and, according to reports from affected users, can result in non-delivery reports with error codes related to SPF (Sender Policy Framework) validation failures. Other users have reported errors highlighting a lack of DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) information. The troubles began at the end of last week and appear to be the result of Microsoft tightening the rules (or at least attempting to do so) for accepting emails. The company's consumer email services are affected, and it appears that if a domain doesn't have working SPF or if it has a missing DMARC record, then Outlook.com and its ilk will treat it as suspicious and not accept emails. The rules are designed to deal with spam, bulk senders, and the like. In 2025, Microsoft announced new rules designed to strengthen email authentication for domains sending more than 5,000 emails per day. In addition to DMARC and SPF compliance, DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) was also required . Although this seemed like a good idea to ward off spammers, small senders now appear to be affected. According to complainants in the Outlook forum, a single email with just one line might now be rejected. Furthermore, Microsoft has not issued any advisory to customers explaining how the rules have changed. Although some customers insist their DMARC, SPF, and DKIM settings are compliant, many more have reported that once they set them to Microsoft's preferences, email began flowing once more. SPF must pass for the sending domain (the domain's DNS record should accurately list authorized IP addresses/hosts). DKIM must pass to validate email integrity and authenticity. DMARC must have at least p=none and align with either SPF or DKIM (preferably both). The Register asked the Windows giant for more information, but we have yet to receive a response. To make matters worse, the glitch also appears to be intermittent. A resend attempt might succeed following a rejection. To compound the situation, the rejection error message may also be vague about what caused the bounce in the first place. A moderator in Microsoft's support forum acknowledged the bug and said it was "classified as a service degradation." "Microsoft is actively investigating the underlying cause of this email delivery issue, and engineering teams are actively analyzing service telemetry and customer-provided data to identify the source of the issue." Still. It could be worse. Earlier today, several users in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa were affected by another Microsoft whoopsie – a "recent service change" that caused some connections to be abruptly terminated. Outlook on the web, as well as the Purview and Defender portals were all affected. Microsoft reverted the change in the Exchange Online front-end infrastructure, and all was well. It has yet to say what else, if anything, might have changed in it

item.title: 2027: INEC condemns ‘rig and die’ slogan, vows sanctions for electoral offenders
item.description: . Seeks media partnership to safeguard democracy . Warns against fake results, inflammatory rhetoric By Steve Oko & Chinedu Adonu The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has condemned the “rig and die” slogan being popularised by some political actors ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that it could expose innocent Nigerians to electoral violence. The Commission also vowed that any electoral official, including ad hoc personnel, found to have compromised the electoral process would face the full weight of the law. INEC National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, gave the warnings at a media engagement forum for journalists and media executives from the South-East, South-South and South-West geopolitical zones in Enugu. Haruna cautioned politicians against inflammatory rhetoric and threats capable of endangering ordinary Nigerians engaged as presiding officers, ad hoc staff, party agents and election observers. He stressed that disagreements over electoral outcomes should be resolved through lawful channels, including complaints to INEC, security agencies and the courts, rather than violence. The National Commissioner also sought stronger collaboration with the media to safeguard democracy and ensure credible, peaceful and transparent conduct of the 2027 elections. Describing the media as critical to electoral credibility, he said public confidence in the electoral process depended largely on the accuracy, fairness and professionalism of election reporting. He cautioned journalists against spreading misinformation, unverified results, manipulated videos and inflammatory political narratives capable of undermining public confidence and triggering violence. Haruna particularly warned against premature declaration of results, sensational reporting and presenting projections as official results. “Results are declared only by the Commission through its duly appointed returning officers. Projections and unofficial figures must be clearly labelled as such,” he said. He urged journalists to verify allegations against INEC through its official channels before publication and report electoral incidents with sensitivity, distinguishing between events personally witnessed and information obtained from other sources. The National Commissioner further called for inclusive election reporting that gives adequate attention to women, youths and persons with disabilities, particularly the challenges they face in participating in the electoral process. He urged media organisations to intensify voter education, especially on Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), accreditation procedures, electronic transmission of results and peaceful participation. item.title: CHOGM 2026: Bianca seeks stronger commonwealth cooperation
item.description: Nigeria has called for stronger cooperation among Commonwealth member states to address security challenges, expand trade, strengthen democratic institutions and promote climate resilience. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, disclosed this on Monday in a post on her X account, detailing Nigeria’s expectations from the Commonwealth following her interventions at the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua. She said Nigeria emphasised the need for collective action on peace and security, trade, climate resilience and youth empowerment, particularly in combating terrorism and expanding access to development finance. Odumegwu-Ojukwu also drew attention to Nigeria’s preparations for the 2027 general elections, stressing the importance of supporting free, fair and credible electoral processes through election monitoring groups and stronger democratic institutions across member states. According to her, Nigeria, under President Bola Tinubu’s leadership, remains committed to promoting democracy, consensus, civil, political and social rights, while upholding the rule of law and judicial independence. She described the creation of the Commonwealth Trade Portal as a welcome development, noting that trade facilitation initiatives would promote economic growth, strengthen trade links among member states and help developing economies integrate into the global financial market. The minister further urged the Commonwealth to give greater attention to women and girls affected by conflicts, displacement and climate change. She said their access to essential services, livelihood opportunities and justice should remain central to collective responses, adding that their voices must shape solutions to the challenges they face. On reparatory justice, Odumegwu-Ojukwu identified the agenda as a major highlight of the ministerial meeting, particularly the agreement by the United Kingdom government to engage in structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected countries over the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical consequences. She said Nigeria hoped that the commitments adopted at CHOGM 2026 would translate into practical actions capable of creating jobs, strengthening security and improving the lives of citizens across Commonwealth member states. item.title: PFIPC Scandal: FG Files Fresh Amended Charges Against Adeyemi Adeniyi, Four Others
item.description: The Federal Government has filed a fresh 36-count amended charge against the embattled Director-General of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Adeyemi Adeniyi, and four others over alleged forgery, false representation and fraud. Adeniyi appeared alongside his co-defendants before Justice Halilu Yusuf of the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Maitama, Abuja, on Monday. However, their arraignment on the fresh charges could not proceed due to the absence of the fourth defendant, Florence Omemah, who was reportedly ill. Prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, informed the court that Ms Omemah was receiving treatment at a hospital in Abuja. He subsequently requested a seven-day adjournment to enable her to recover and appear in court to take her plea. Counsel to Mr Adeniyi, Ibrahim Angulu, however, urged the court to grant a shorter adjournment to allow him to pursue bail for his client. He also told the court that Mr Adeniyi had been in detention for more than 200 days. In a brief ruling, Justice Yusuf adjourned the case until November 18 for the arraignment of all the defendants. The judge further ordered that Mr Adeniyi be remanded at the Kuje Correctional Centre, while the other defendants should remain in the custody of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC). Alleged Fake Government Agency Adeniyi Adeyemi paraded himself as the DG of the PFIPC. Photo: X@BayoOnanuga. The case centres on allegations that Adeniyi established a fictitious federal agency known as the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council and falsely presented himself as its director-general. Investigators alleged that the agency had no legal backing and that Mr Adeniyi forged appointment letters and signatures attributed to the Chief of Staff to the President to legitimise his purported position. According to investigators, he occupied offices previously used by the defunct Presidential Economic Advisory Council at the Federal Secretariat in Abuja and allegedly held unauthorised meetings with foreign diplomats. He was also accused of seeking official visa documentation for United States visas and operating 34 bank accounts. Investigators further alleged that he exploited loopholes in the civil service system to secure a proposed allocation of ₦1.302 billion for the fictitious agency in the 2026 budget. ICPC Uncovers Other Alleged Fake Agencies Following an interim report presented to President Bola Tinubu, the ICPC reportedly uncovered two other allegedly fictitious agencies linked to Mr Adeniyi: the FCT Investment Promotion Agency and the Foreign Investment Promotion Agency. The commission also recommended disciplinary action against some public officials suspected of assisting the alleged scheme. In October 2026, the Federal High Court in Abuja struck out the initial eight-count charge after jurisdictional concerns prompted the Attorney-General of the Federation to withdraw the case. item.title: Musiala’s condition cannot be cured, may never return to best — Bayern president
item.description: Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeness has raised concerns over Jamal Musiala’s long-term future, saying the Germany international is suffering from a condition that cannot be permanently cured and may never regain his previous level of performance. According to BBC Sport, Hoeness said the 23-year-old forward’s condition could only be managed to some extent with medication, leaving the club uncertain about whether he would return to his best. “We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,” Hoeness told Bavarian broadcaster BR24. He also questioned whether Musiala would ever recover the level he displayed before his health problems, while acknowledging that Bayern would continue to support the player, who is under contract until 2030. “But the question remains: will he one day be able to regain the level he used to show?” Hoeness said. Hoeness further suggested that the situation had created a contractual dilemma for the German champions, claiming Musiala’s condition was not covered by the insurance attached to his deal. “Imagine if Bayern Munich now decided to question his contract, and told him: what you are able to offer currently no longer matches the level stipulated in the contract,” he said. Musiala’s health concerns emerged during pre-season after he collapsed twice within four days. He was subsequently reported to have a treatable neurological dysfunction. The forward has also been sidelined by a hamstring injury sustained in September and has yet to feature for Bayern since then, although he has recently returned to training. He has scored twice in four appearances for the German champions in all competitions this season. Former Bayern and Germany captain Lothar Matthaus, however, interpreted Hoeness’ comments as an attempt to challenge and motivate the youngster rather than write him off. “He’s needling him a little. It’s not just about wrapping him in cotton wool. He also has to battle against adversity sometimes,” Matthaus told Sky90. Matthaus added that Hoeness wanted Musiala to respond to the remarks by proving he could return to his previous level. “Uli was looking to create that adversity with this statement. “It’s fine for him to say something like that, because we can’t just put a positive spin on things and somehow wait for him to come back. “If I were in Jamal Musiala’s position, that would be motivation enough to show Uli I’m back.” Musiala joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea’s academy and has since scored 71 goals and provided 38 assists in 235 appearances for the club. He has earned 46 caps for Germany and shared the Golden Boot as joint-top scorer at Euro 2024. Vanguard News The post Musiala’s condition cannot be cured, may never return to best — Bayern president appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Who can still open your files after they've left?
item.description: Someone left your organisation in the spring. Can they still open the project share? Most infrastructure leads would want to check before answering, and that pause is the subject of a dinner The Register and LucidLink are hosting for senior technology, infrastructure and data leaders at the Covent Garden Hotel on Tuesday 24 November. Joe Fay of The Register is in the chair. Request a place The trouble is the copies. A busy folder lives on the file server, in a sync client, on a couple of laptops and in the share set up for an agency last year, and each copy carries its own permissions. Locking down one leaves the others as they were. Then there's the tool a team built for itself because the approved one was too slow, which IT may not know exists. The evening runs under the Chatham House Rule, and that's what makes it worth going. People say what actually happened in their own shop and how they caught it. Alan Marshall, Strategic Director, EMEA at LucidLink, joins a small group of peers round the table. Nobody presents. The talk moves on to unstructured data that keeps growing, the duplicate storage that comes with it, and how to get access back under control without throwing out the storage and governance you've already paid for. Drinks are at 6.30pm and dinner around one table runs until 9pm. Places are limited. Request a place at the 24 November dinner Places go by invitation and each one is confirmed personally. Sponsored by LucidLink.

item.title: NASA unveils $10 billion in moon base contracts, new lunar missions and the 'PROMISE' of a nuclear-powered rover
item.description: null CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA is pushing ahead with its plan to build a moon base for astronauts by 2032, with the agency unveiling up to $10 billion in contracts to launch and deliver cargo to the moon and other efforts on Saturday (Nov. 7). The NASA announcement, revealed here during the space agency's "Max Power" air show event at Kennedy Space Center , included plans for a new $10 billion Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) framework, dubbed CLPS 2, about$1.3 billion in funding for the agency's Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare (VADR) program, and the nuclear-powered "PROMISE" rover on the moon. The announcements mark another step in NASA's effort to establish infrastructure on the moon before Artemis astronauts return to its surface, including a rover and other cargo and research elements. "Under the current CLPS contract, it's all all or nothing, which might be fine if you're only doing one or two of those [missions] per year," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman told Space.com during a press conference on Saturday. "But when you're trying to scale up to what we're talking about today, you want to have the flexibility to move pieces around." Landing cargo on the moon NASA selected eight companies to compete for the new CLPS 2 missions under the framework: Blue Origin , Firefly Aerospace, Intuitive Machines, ispace-U.S., Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, SpaceX and Voyager Technologies. The contracts for the 10-year CLPS 2 architecture carry a combined maximum value of $10 billion, rather than $10 billion in immediately awarded missions. NASA also increased the ceiling of its existing CLPS contract from $2.6 billion to $4.2 billion to support the agency's "Phase One" Moon Base objectives. NASA is also following through on a promise Isaacman made in June, when he proposed repurposing an engineering model of the Perseverance and Curiosity Mars rovers (essentially an Earth-based twin) as a mission-ready rover to send to the moon. That rover, called PROMISE (short for "Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration"), is a nuclear-powered robot intended to explore the lunar south pole beginning in late 2028. The autonomous rover will carry a drill and scientific instruments to search for volatiles and water ice on the lunar surface. NASA awarded Blue Origin a $94 million base contract, with an additional $140 million option period based on performance, to deliver PROMISE to the lunar surface aboard its Blue Moon Mark 1 lander . Communication satellites, navigation tests and more In addition to that contract for Blue Origin, NASA awarded six launch and orbital transportation task orders worth a total of approximately $1.3 billion to Arrow Science and Technology, Blue Origin and Impulse Space under its Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare (VADR) program. The missions will demonstrate commercial launch and orbital transportation capabilities, including cargo transfers between Earth and lunar

item.title: NASA chief Jared Isaacman skydives into space agency's MAX POWER air show — 'Going into this job, I knew we had to do something like this.'
item.description: null CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman knows how to make an entrance. Under the bright afternoon sun on Saturday (Nov. 7), Isaacman plummeted through the air above 10,000 onlookers, skydiving into the agency's air show MAX POWER. MAX POWER overtook NASA's Kennedy Space Center here over the weekend, combining aeronautics and aerospace in a massive public air show, the first of its kind for the space agency. A mix of astronauts, fighter jet displays and new technology on display, the spectacle is a lot space-ier than a traditional air show, and Isaacman made sure to really showcase this merging of worlds. A pilot and private astronaut, Jared Isaacman is no stranger to the skies, and immediately after landing back on solid ground he jumped right back up and took to the event's main stage to greet an excited crowd. "Going into this job, I I knew we had to do something like this," Isaacman said after landing and taking the stage. "We knew on our nation's 250th birthday , we had to open up [the] Kennedy Space Center the year that we returned our astronauts to the lunar environment and put on a little bit of a show." NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman jumps out of an airplane with members of the Chicago Skydive team. Space.com’s super zoomed-in photo of this jump was made possible by a Canon R5 Mark II camera , with an RF 200-800mm lens. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) EOS R5 Mark II: $3999 This mirrorless Canon has specs that make it one of the best cameras available right now, with impressive features and functionality, including a 45MP sensor and excellent high-ISO handling. Check our in-depth Canon R5 Mark II review . View Deal And put on a show he did. From thousands of feet above a crowd holding their breath, Isaacman jumped out of a plane alongside members of Skydive Chicago and other notable individuals, including Montana senator Tim Sheehy (R-Montana) and former U.S. Air Force Thunderbird pilot Shawn Gustoson. One by one, tiny white parachutes popped up in the sky above, which continued to grow in size as the skydivers neared the ground. And before we knew it, Isaacman was gracefully touching down just behind the air show's main stage, landing to the sound of cheers from the eager audience. In addition to serving in his role as NASA Administrator, Isaacman is an entrepreneur, commercial astronaut and pilot. Known in flight by his callsign "Rook" which he was given during fighter jet training, Isaacman has so far logged over 8,000 flight hours. In 2009, he broke the world record for fastest trip around the world in a light jet (he made the trip in 61 hours, 51 minutes and 15 seconds) and is flight-qualified in a number of military jet aircraft. He also financed and flew on two private orbital space missions on a SpaceX Dragon, Inspiration4 and Polaris Dawn , performing the world's first private spacewalk on the latter misison. item.title: Japanese homeware giant pulls online store after cloud breach puts 7.7M records at risk
item.description: Japanese electronics giant Iris Ohyama has taken down its online store after discovering that attackers may have accessed the personal information of 7.7 million customers, leaving shoppers unable to place orders. The retailer, which sells everything from home appliances and furniture to pet supplies, first disclosed the incident on October 29 , a day after discovering a suspicious file on a third-party cloud service used by its Iris Plaza ecommerce operation. Iris Plaza immediately suspended its website and associated systems and began investigating, subsequently confirming unauthorized access. Iris Ohyama has since revealed that the potentially compromised cloud environment contained personal information belonging to approximately 5.8 million registered customers, including former members, and another 1.9 million people who had purchased products without creating an account or participated in promotional campaigns. The potentially exposed information includes names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, gender, and passwords, although the company says the exact information at risk varies between customers. Some of that data, including passwords, was encrypted, but Iris Ohyama hasn't explained what protection was used. It has advised customers who reused their Iris Plaza passwords elsewhere to change them, presumably before someone else gets the opportunity. There is some good news for anyone who has handed over their credit card details, as the retailer says it didn't store payment information in the affected cloud service and that it hasn't been compromised. It remains unclear whether the attackers actually made off with any personal information. In its FAQ , Iris Plaza says it is still investigating the possibility of a data leak and has yet to establish the full extent of the intrusion. Meanwhile, Iris Plaza's website is still down, and the company isn't saying when it'll be back. Orders are also taking longer to ship, while customers trying to cancel a purchase have been told they may have to turn the delivery driver away if their parcel arrives before the cancellation is processed. Fortunately for anyone desperate to buy a new rice cooker, Iris Plaza's stores on Rakuten, Yahoo! Shopping, and auPAY Market are still operating. The company says it has found no evidence that those stores were affected. Iris Ohyama has reported the incident to Japanese authorities and says it will contact potentially affected customers individually. It has also warned shoppers to watch out for phishing emails, fraudulent calls, and fake websites impersonating the retailer. The company has yet to identify the cloud provider involved, explain how the attackers got in, or establish whether any of those 7.7 million records actually left its systems. ®

item.title: Israel Olaleye: What Selling Land Taught Me About How Nigerians Think About Money
item.description: In 2021, I graduated from the University of Ibadan with a degree in Mathematics. I thought my life would be about numbers on a whiteboard. I did not know it would become about numbers in people’s bank accounts, and the fears, hopes and contradictions that sit behind them. By mid-2023, I had taken a job selling real estate. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. You can earn a lot and still not be wealthy One idea I keep returning to is that you can earn twenty million naira a year and still not be wealthy. Income is what comes in. Wealth is what stays and grows. Two people can earn the same salary and end up in completely different places ten years later, simply because one converted part of that income into assets and the other converted all of it into lifestyle. Wealthy people do not always look wealthy. Some of the most financially secure people I have met do not drive the loudest cars. And some of the people who look the richest are one bad month away from panic. So the question I now ask myself, and the people I speak with, is simple: what exactly are you converting your income into? Real estate is bigger than land and a house One conversation changed how I explain property to people. A Nigerian living in Canada called me after watching a video I had made about a commercial development in Ibadan. A few minutes in, he said something I have since heard from many people: “To me, real estate has always mean

item.description: Hey, did you hear about those elections in the US this past week? You can listen to the latest episode of The Kettle right here on this page, as well as on Spotify , Apple Music , or YouTube . Those platforms also let you subscribe to The Kettle, so you are always notified when the latest episode goes live. The Democratic party has seized control of Congress and state governments around the country. It's easy to see this entirely as a rebuke of Trump and his policies, but blowback against AI, datacenters, and the tech industry played a role too, if the past week of chaos in markets and Silicon Valley is any indication. Join host Brandon Vigliarolo , El Reg Editor In Chief Matt Rosoff , and special guest, senior reporter at The Verge, Elizabeth Lopatto , to talk about what the winds of political change mean for the tech industry. A lightly edited transcript is below: Brandon (00:04) Hey everyone, and welcome to the latest episode of The Register' s Kettle Podcast. I'm your host, Reg Reporter Brandon Vigliarolo, and hey, chances are you've heard about those elections we had in the US this week. The Democratic Party dealt a pretty hearty rebuke to Donald Trump, Republicans, and the MAGA movement, with Dems winning elections in states that haven't gone blue in decades. Now it's easy to see this as a blowback against Trump and Republican politics. There's a lot of indication that the tech industry was kind of on the ballot this year, too. After all, they cozied up hard to Trump in his first two years in office in a bid to push AI and promote datacenter projects, and people have been none too happy about any of that. With me to discuss the elections and what they mean for Silicon Valley is Reg editor-in-chief Matt Rosoff and a special guest this week, senior reporter from The Verge, Elizabeth Lopatto. Thank you both for coming on, and welcome, Liz. Liz (00:53) Thank you. It's lovely to be here. Brandon (00:54) I was so glad we could make this work. So let's start off by dissecting the degree to which AI datacenters and attitudes toward the tech industry in general sort of played a role in this election. I mean, were those major elements in the Democratic sweep or just part of the equation? Liz (01:13) I think they were part of the equation. I think first and foremost people were pissed off about the corruption. And second, people were pissed off about ICE. Having people snatched from your community is the sort of thing that kind of sticks with you. So I think those were probably the two biggest issues. But the corruption is not totally separate from the tech industry, given the way that the tech industry has been cozying up with Donald Trump, the fact that Elon Musk and DOGE were cruising through the federal government, destroying stuff. So those things are related. And then obviously there's the datacenter stuff, which is universally unpopular, not the only bipartisan issue in the US right now, but certainly a big one. So it's in there, I think. Matt

item.title: AI echo chambers and sanity in tech leadership: Three case studies
item.description: "AI delusion" remains loosely defined, but most of us know it when we see it: exaggerated faith in the technology's power, applicability, or nature, coupled with a refusal to acknowledge its limitations. It's bad in the individual, as when an elderly relative emails you a hallucination-laden ChatGPT summary. It's worse in management, when your boss insists that AI slop is genius marketing content at a bargain rate. It is terrifying in tech CEOs. It is not, thankfully, compulsory. Consider three recent examples of technology leadership in the age of AI. One would be Pythonesque were the disconnect with engineers and the public not so profound. Another risks becoming a business-school case study in how to demolish customer trust. The third offers something less fashionable: robust pragmatism. Saving the best till last, y'all. Case 1: we present for your consideration Sam Altman of OpenAI, one of the few actually at the controls of the singularity machine. It seems churlish to pluck just one luscious fruit out of that cornucopia of choices, yet we must. Sam Altman thinks it is a sin against the natural order that so much RAM is idling in machines owned by individuals, organizations, and anywhere that isn't Big AI . It's oh so inefficient. How convenient that the efficient allocation of scarce resources should favor the business he runs. Free market schmarket. Altman has since said his remarks were taken out of context and that he wants consumers to have as much memory as they like. The efficiency argument still reveals whose priorities come first. This is the best kind of delusion, one with an undeniable truth at its core – memory does indeed get used far more intensively in AI model makers and inference servers than in your laptop. For a business selling the future, treating privately owned hardware as an inefficient allocation of resources has a distinctly Soviet flavor, and the American right has vowed to stamp out socialist extremism. Get on with it, chaps, you've only got two years left . That Altman can't see this is the best bit of the misconception. There are two potential root causes of this Marxist-Leninist-Altmanism. One is that he's mathed the math and worked out that the only way OpenAI can hit the numbers is if it gets every last byte in the world, hot off the fab. The other is that you can't run on-prem on an 8 GB state-mandated Chromebook, and on-prem is otherwise going to twist his melon until it falls off. Case 2: Andy Yen, CEO of Proton, the company behind Proton Mail and Proton VPN. You, me, and the household cat know ProtonMail as the secondary email that's worth paying for. You want the best recovery backup email for Gmail, you want it as an accessible end-to-end encrypted email service. You want it because it is all about stable spotless security, all about the end users, all about being there when you absolutely need it. It is safe to recommend, and you do. Or rather that's what you thought about ProtonMail et al until the sa

item.title: DisCos Apologise To Nigerians Over Power Outages
item.description: Electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) have apologised to Nigerians over persistent electricity shortages across the country, acknowledging the hardship caused by weeks of prolonged blackouts. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Association of Nigerian Electricity Distributors (ANED), Sunday Oduntan, tendered the apology on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . “I’d like to first of all start by apologising to Nigerians. Apology is needed; it is essential because Nigerians have been taken through this problem over the past few weeks,” he said. Oduntan also criticised what he described as a return to the blame game among operators in the electricity sector, recalling that similar disagreements between stakeholders had characterised the industry between 2016 and 2019. He said distribution companies, transmission operators, generation companies and gas suppliers had previously blamed one another for poor electricity supply instead of addressing the underlying problems. “Our major problem is that we have started that very wrong route that we went through between 2016 and 2019. What is that? Blame game. “Part of what happened at that time is that people will blame the DisCos, DisCos will blame TCN, TCN will blame GenCos, GenCos will blame the gas suppliers, and gas suppliers will blame payment issues. We have returned to that, and I think there is a need to arrest that,” he said. Oduntan Questions Conflicting Explanations A combo of the Chief Executive Officer of the Association of Nigerian Electricity Distributors (ANED), Sunday Oduntan and electricity installations. The ANED spokesperson also expressed concern over statements issued by the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) regarding the factors responsible for the electricity shortages. He said NISO had attributed the supply challenges partly to low water levels and inadequate gas supply, while the NNPC subsequently issued a statement indicating that gas was available. Oduntan, however, questioned the information provided by the national oil company, insisting that it should clarify whether outstanding payments were affecting gas supply to power generation companies. “From the NNPC statement, it is very clear that they came to tell us half-truths. What I would have expected NNPC to do is to go ahead and talk to us whether there are payment issues. We need to know whether gas was paid for and delivered, who did, who didn’t,” he said. The ANED CEO urged the Minister of Power to intervene by bringing the relevant stakeholders together to establish the actual causes of the shortages. “This back and forth blame game between gas suppliers, NNPC and, of course, TCN or NISO, I think the Minister of Power needs to take charge. item.title: Portal breach at Germany's top university exposes every registered user's password
item.description: Attackers stole central university login passwords belonging to everyone registered with the Technical University of Munich's myTUM portal, including an admin whose credentials were then used to attack a second system. TUM restored access to its TUMonline campus management system on Monday morning, allowing users to change their passwords. The university disclosed the attack on November 6. The initial attack targeted the myTUM portal, which serves students and faculty members, providing centralized online access to services and documents. TUM said the attackers used the admin's credentials to launch a follow-on attack on TUMonline, its central campus management system, which forced the IT team to take it offline. The university has not disclosed how the attackers initially gained access or how the stolen passwords were stored. It did not immediately answer questions about the number of affected users. It also did not specify whether this sysadmin had multi-factor authentication (MFA) switched on, but it confirmed that "user accounts with MFA were protected from this attack." Attackers may also have accessed names, home addresses, and dates of birth. Potentially exposed employee records included work addresses and phone numbers, while student records included ID numbers, degree programs, and completed semesters. "The attackers' access within TUMonline was largely logged," said Dr Alexander Braun, CIO at TUM, in the disclosure. "After analyzing these logs, we currently assume that no other data from TUMonline was compromised, such as grades or college applications. We are continuing to investigate this." TUM is directing users to reset their passwords through Microsoft 365 where possible. Those without MFA already configured must instead use a German electronic ID or request a reset email while connected to the campus network. The university also warned users to watch for phishing and fraud, and to change any passwords reused elsewhere. TUM ranks first in Germany and 25th worldwide in the QS university rankings. The STEM-focused institution reports 51,954 students across its German campuses and TUM Asia in Singapore, plus 12,850 employees. ®

item.title: CHAPEA Mission 2 Crew Reflects After 378 Days on Simulated Mars
item.description: 6 Min Read CHAPEA Mission 2 Crew Reflects After 378 Days on Simulated Mars The CHAPEA (Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog) Mission 2 crew egress from their simulated Mars habitat, completing their mission on Oct. 31, 2026, at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Credits: NASA/James Blair After 378 days without windows, the sounds of the outside world, or real-time calls with family and friends, four research volunteers stepped out of NASA’s Mars Dune Alpha habitat on Oct. 31, completing the agency’s second yearlong Mars surface simulation. Ross Elder, Ellen Ellis, James Spicer, and Matthew Montgomery entered the roughly 1,700-square-foot, 3D-printed habitat at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston on Oct. 19, 2025, for CHAPEA (Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog) Mission 2. The crew participated in simulated Marswalks, robotic operations, habitat maintenance, exercise, and crop cultivation. “Their work means more than completing a mission,” said Johnson Director Vanessa Wyche. “It is about preparing for the challenges of human exploration beyond Earth, gathering the knowledge we need to protect crew health and performance, and paving the way for future missions to the Moon and, one day, Mars.” Family, friends, and colleagues welcome the CHAPEA Mission 2 crew as they exit the building housing the Mars Dune Alpha habitat on Oct. 31, 2026. NASA/James Blair NASA astronaut Jack Hathaway put the crew’s time in isolation into perspective: While they were inside the habitat, he completed a 237-day mission aboard the space station and returned to Earth. During that same period, the Artemis II astronauts traveled around the Moon and set the record for the farthest humans have traveled from Earth. NASA also celebrated 25 years of continuous human presence aboard the International Space Station on Nov. 2, 2025. “The reality of what you guys did here required immense physiological and psychological strength, teamwork, and human grit,” Hathaway said. Supported by researchers and ground teams across the agency, the CHAPEA crew collected health and performance data while navigating limited resources and communication delays of up to 22 minutes each way. Ross Elder: Commander and Test Pilot Ross Elder, CHAPEA Mission 2 commander, prepares for a simulated Marswalk in the habitat’s airlock. Elder brought a U.S. Air Force experimental test pilot’s approach to leading the crew. He found simulated Marswalks and robotic exploration “uncannily similar” to operating as part of a flight. From inside the habitat, crew members remotely operated a drone and a rover to survey terrain and identify or collect rock samples. The demanding Marswalk schedule also sharpened his understanding of the physical preparation future explorers will need. Preparing suits, completing airlock procedures, and making long traverses took time and stamina. He emphasized nutrition, exercise, and rest as essential to sustaining that pace. item.title: Yes, it runs 'Doom': Satellite plays iconic game in world's 1st demonstration of orbital voice control
item.description: null A satellite went knee-deep in the dead, after a voice command from the ground activated the Doom video game in space. Playing a first-person shooter from 1993 was obviously not in the design plan for the PRETTY cubesat , which is run by a consortium including the European Space Agency (ESA). But the pioneering voice command opens up new worlds for satellite work, the team says. "Someone in distress at sea or in a remote area could transmit 'mayday' or "help" on a radio," stated Estonia's Tanagra Space, which supplied the software for the feat. The hope is one day, a satellite could use transcription and AI to alert rescue services for assisting folks in remote zones. The call to play Doom, thankfully, had no other urgency than curiosity — and teamwork, fueled by pizza. OPS-SAT Space Lab managed the experiment on behalf of ESA. Radio amateurs then made six unsuccessful attempts during passes over Poland and Norway, between April and July. The seventh finally reached success under the Oslo Group of the Norwegian Radio Relay League. "We are radio amateurs, with the emphasis on amateurs. Satellite work was not something our club did, and we had no budget for it," representative Eskil Hadland, call sign LB6AJ, said in the Tangara statement. "So we borrowed a line wrongly credited to Pippi Longstocking: 'I have never tried that before, so I should definitely be able to do that.'" The Norwegians spent 59 days and about 7200 NOK or $775 (pizza included) to reach PRETTY, helping make changes to the satellite software to pick up a voice. For example, a raw recording of an attempt on July 3, retransmitted to Earth, showed the spoken words to space were unrecognizable. Further work revealed the satellite's receiver channel was too wide to pick up the voice signal, leading to a fix to narrow the channel. The historic voice command on July 27— in part, "PRETTY play Doom Doom Doom"— came from a rooftop in Oslo, and was spoken at night by Jon Bergli Heier (LB9BJ). PRETTY picked up the transmission, transcribed the command using on-board voice recognition, and then — just like a typical evening gamer—opened up Doom for a play session. A member of the LB9BJ team speaks the command that activated Doom on the OPS-SAT PRETTY satellite while on a rooftop in Oslo, Norway during an evening pass of the spacecraft on July 27, 2026. (Image credit: Truls Johansen (LA7IJ), LA4O) This was no multiplayer gaming situation, but the satellite did create a report of its demon-slaying skills — and its ability to interpret the command. For example, PRETTY generated a "postcard" including a frame of the gameplay, a transcription, and signal diagnostics. The satellite also transmitted its recording of Hadland's command. As anybody who uses voice-recognition software knows, there are challenges in transcriptions: nobody speaks in exactly the same way, and aspects such as accent or background noise can lead to misinterpretations. The satellite also had to contend with Doppler shift
